title: fix duplicate EasyEDA pad connectivity
description: Fixes the issue of duplicate EasyEDA pad connectivity by ensuring that multiple geometries with the same pad number are treated as a single logical pin, eliminating synthetic ports and ambiguous connections.
body: ## Problem The EasyEDA converter treated every physical `PAD` geometry as a separate logical pin, even when several geometries had the same EasyEDA pad number. That produced synthetic source ports and duplicate aliases which do not exist on the component. For `C132561`, the source footprint contains eleven physical pad geometries: - signal pads `1` through `5` - six shell geometries, all numbered `6` The old conversion incorrectly emitted logical `pin6` through `pin11`. Pins `7`–`11` all received the same `pin6_alt1` alias, so the generated component had ambiguous, invented ports. EasyEDA pad numbers map footprint geometry to schematic pins. Multiple geometries carrying the same pad number therefore belong to the same logical terminal; they are not additional source pins. See the [EasyEDA footprint documentation](https://docs.easyeda.com/en/PCBLib/PCBLib-Create/). ## Before and after snapshots | `C132561` | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Physical pad geometries | 11 | 11 | | Logical source ports | 11 | 6 | | Shell geometries | `pin6`–`pin11` | six shapes on `pin6` | | Synthetic ports | `pin7`–`pin11` | none | ### Rendered regression snapshots The visual fixture below is `C51950748`, which has nine physical exposed-pad geometries sharing EasyEDA pad number 29. The **before** images were rendered from base commit `2ef5112`; the **after** images were rendered from this PR at `74e921d`. #### Schematic | Before — invented pins 33–40 | After — one logical `EPAD` pin 29 | | --- | --- | | | | Before the fix, the repeated pad number created synthetic schematic pins 33–40 with the duplicate `pin29_alt1` label. After the fix, the schematic exposes one logical `EPAD` terminal at pin 29. #### PCB | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | The PCB geometry is intentionally unchanged: all nine center copper pads remain. The fix changes their logical mapping so every center shape belongs to `pin29`; it does not remove or merge physical copper. ### Before ```tsx const pinLabels = { pin6: ["EH1"], pin7: ["pin6_alt1"], pin8: ["pin6_alt1"], pin9: ["pin6_alt1"], pin10: ["pin6_alt1"], pin11: ["pin6_alt1"], } // Six shell geometries were incorrectly assigned different logical ports. ``` ### After ```tsx const pinLabels = { pin6: ["EH"], } // The same six physical geometries correctly share logical pin 6. ``` The repeated `` entries above are physical copper shapes, not duplicate source ports. ## Root cause `convertEasyEdaJsonToCircuitJson` passed one label set per physical pad into `normalizePinLabels`. The normalizer avoided duplicate canonical pin numbers by renumbering later occurrences, so repeated pad numbers became synthetic pins. ## Fix - group numbered EasyEDA pad geometries by their original pad number before normalization - normalize each logical pad-number group once - emit one `source_port` per logical pin - preserve every physical SMT/plated-hole geometry and map each one back to its shared logical pin - keep unnumbered pads independent - add regression coverage using a real component with a split exposed pad - snapshot both schematic and PCB rendering for the repeated-pad fixture - update the affected `C2838502`, `C2913206`, and `C51950748` generated snapshots ## Impact Generated imports no longer expose invented or ambiguous pins. Split exposed pads, shell tabs, and other multi-geometry terminals retain all footprint copper while matching the logical connectivity declared by the EasyEDA source. ## Validation - `bunx tsc --noEmit` - `bun run build` - `bun run format:check` - `git diff --check` - focused regression suite: 12 passed, 0 failed - live `C132561` conversion: one logical `pin6` across six shell geometries - visual regression: one schematic `EPAD` terminal while all nine PCB pad shapes remain - all GitHub CI checks passed Fixes #411. This is a fresh-`main` replacement for #413, which currently conflicts with `main`. It follows the same source-pad semantics while using an existing real component fixture for regression coverage.

title: Infer pin attributes for imported chips
description: Infers conservative pin attributes for imported chip power, ground, and no-connect pins, emitting the inferred attributes in generated tscircuit components while skipping ambiguous or unsupported aliases.
body:
## Summary

- infer conservative `pinAttributes` for imported chip power, ground, and no-connect pins
- emit the inferred attributes in generated tscircuit components
- skip ambiguous or unsupported aliases rather than guessing
- update converter snapshots and add unit plus circuit-JSON integration coverage

## Why

EasyEDA imports previously emitted pin labels without electrical pin metadata. As a result, tscircuit checks reported imported IC pins as underspecified even when their labels clearly identified supply, ground, or no-connect pins.

## Impact

Imported chips now mark recognized `VCC`, `VDD`, `VIN`, and `VDDA` pins as requiring power; `GND`, `VSS`, `PGND`, and `AGND` pins as requiring ground; and `NC` pins as do-not-connect. Numbered variants are supported, while ambiguous multi-label pins remain unchanged.

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- `bun test` — 178 passed, 0 failed; 59 snapshots; 795 expectations
- `git diff --check`

title: Fix JLCPCB keyboard switches importing as malformed chips
description: Fixes JLCPCB mechanical keyboard switch imports that are incorrectly generated as generic chip components with malformed schematic symbols.
body:
## Summary

Fixes JLCPCB mechanical keyboard switch imports that are incorrectly generated as generic `<chip>` components with malformed schematic symbols.

## What changed

- Detects keyboard-switch metadata from `KEY-TH_` and `KEY-SMD_` package identifiers.
- Generates `PushButtonProps` and `<pushbutton>` for mechanical keyboard switches.
- Preserves the imported footprint, supplier part number, and CAD model.
- Updates the `C49234237` regression fixture and schematic snapshot.
- Adds classification coverage for keyboard-switch metadata.

## Reproduction

JLCPCB part `C49234237` (`CPG151101D06`, brown mechanical keyboard switch) previously generated:

```tsx
import type { ChipProps } from "@tscircuit/props"

<chip>
```

This produced an oversized, malformed schematic symbol.

The corrected output generates:

```tsx
import type { PushButtonProps } from "@tscircuit/props"

<pushbutton>
```

## Validation

- `bun format`
- Focused `C49234237` conversion test
- Pushbutton category tests
- Updated schematic SVG snapshot

This PR both reproduces and fixes the import-classification and schematic-symbol issue.

## Reproduction

This PR adds a captured EasyEDA fixture and focused regression test for JLCPCB part `C49234237`.

The test documents that the part currently generates a generic `<chip>` instead of a `<pushbutton>` component.

## Root cause observed

`C49234237` does not expose `Mechanical Keyboard Shaft` through the category fields inspected by the converter. Its EasyEDA metadata identifies the part through `pre: KEY?` and `package: KEY-TH_CPG151101D06`, so it was generated as a generic `<chip>` with a malformed schematic symbol.

title: Repro: trailing-hash active-low pin labels lose polarity
description: Adds a regression test to reproduce the issue where active-low pin labels lose their polarity due to the removal of trailing hashes in the conversion process.
body:
## Motivation

The raw EasyEDA data for JLCPCB part C490691 (FT232RL) marks active-low pins with a trailing `#`, including `DTR#`, `RTS#`, `RI#`, and `RESET#`.

The converter currently removes the trailing `#` without preserving its meaning. Generated labels such as `DTR` and `RESET` therefore appear as normal positive-logic signals instead of active-low signals.

![C490691 schematic with stripped active-low labels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/easyeda-converter/codex/repro-active-low-trailing-hash/tests/convert-to-ts/__snapshots__/C490691-active-low-labels-stripped.snap.svg)

## Reproduction

- Confirms the raw EasyEDA source contains `DTR#` and `RESET#`.
- Confirms the generated TSX incorrectly contains `DTR` and `RESET` instead of `N_DTR` and `N_RESET`.
- Adds a schematic snapshot showing that the affected signals are rendered without active-low overlines.

This PR only adds regression coverage and does not implement the fix.

title: Fix document-layer tracks converted to silkscreen
description: Fixes the conversion of EasyEDA document-layer tracks to ensure they are preserved as fabrication notes instead of being incorrectly converted to silkscreen.
body:
## Motivation

EasyEDA Document-layer tracks are currently converted to PCB silkscreen. This can incorrectly add reference-only markings to the manufactured silkscreen.

This change preserves those tracks as fabrication notes, keeping them visible in tscircuit without including them in the physical silkscreen.

## Summary

- restrict EasyEDA TRACK-to-silkscreen conversion to layers 3 and 4
- preserve layer-12 document tracks as fabrication-note paths
- update the regression assertion and PCB SVG snapshots

Fixes the behavior reproduced in #449. The converter previously treated every non-courtyard TRACK as silkscreen; C136720 now keeps its right-side bracket as a visible fabrication note instead.

Verified against the current EasyEDA payload for C136720: two TRACKs are on TopSilkLayer (3), and the right-side bracket is on Document (12).

title: Preserve all pins on multi-pin inductors
description: Fixes the issue where multi-pin inductors were incorrectly converted to two-terminal inductors, resulting in lost physical terminals in the schematic.
body:
## Motivation

bug repro in #461.

[JLCPCB/LCSC C3273487](https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C3273487.html) is a four-pin Bourns SRF1280-101M coupled inductor. It was converted to the two-terminal `<inductor>` primitive, leaving two physical terminals unavailable in the schematic.

## Fix

- Use `<inductor>` only for two-pin inductors.
- Fall back to `<chip>` for multi-pin inductors so every physical terminal remains connectable.
- Avoid embedding the custom EasyEDA symbol for this fallback because combining its ports with `chip.pinLabels` creates duplicate source ports.
- Preserve normal two-pin inductor conversion.

The corrected C3273487 output contains exactly four source ports, four schematic ports, and four PCB pads.

 Corrected schematic 
 ![C3273487 four-terminal schematic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/easyeda-converter/codex/fix-c3273487-coupled-inductor/tests/convert-to-ts/__snapshots__/C3273487-coupled-inductor-chip.snap.svg)

title: Honor pcbStyle via dimensions during autorouting
description: Uses pcbStyle.viaHoleDiameter and pcbStyle.viaPadDiameter as autorouter via constraints when minVia props are not set, ensuring consistent via sizes for both authored and generated vias.
body:
## Summary

- use `pcbStyle.viaHoleDiameter` and `pcbStyle.viaPadDiameter` as autorouter via constraints when `minVia*` props are not set
- keep explicit `minViaHoleDiameter` and `minViaPadDiameter` precedence
- add regression coverage for routed via dimensions and a PCB snapshot

## Why

`pcbStyle` already controls explicit `<via>` dimensions, but autorouted vias were still created with the board's manufacturing defaults. This made one board-level style produce different via sizes depending on whether a via was authored or generated.

The board previously inserted default `min_via_*` values before routed traces were converted to Circuit JSON, so the later `pcbStyle` fallback could never take effect.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test tests/features/pcb-style-via-diameter.test.tsx tests/features/autorouter-inferred-min-via-pad-diameter.test.tsx tests/features/autorouter-min-via-dimensions.test.tsx tests/features/autorouter-pcb-style-via-diameter.test.tsx`

body:
Fills in the gaps recorded by the base PR, and re-renders **the same snapshots from the same cameras**. Where they showed bare copper pads they now show the part; that diff is the review. The ledger goes from 35 entries to 3.

Most of this is dispatch, not geometry. `lib/Footprinter3d.tsx` switches on footprinter's `fn` and simply had no arm for these names, while a suitable body sat in `lib/` unreferenced — `SOT-563.tsx` and `BGA.tsx` had never been reachable at all, SC-70-4 shares SC-70-6's body, SOP and SSOP are SOIC with a different lead span, SON/WSON/VSON are DFNs, MLP and QUAD are QFNs.

Parameterised rather than aliased wherever the outline genuinely differs, since an alias reports a body that is not there:

- `SOT-223` takes its dimensions, so SOT-89 can use it at a third of the volume
- `TO-220` takes `mouldedTab`, because TO-220F encapsulates the tab
- LGA/MLP/QUAD read `w`/`h`, **not** `grid`: for those `grid` is a pad COUNT per side (`lga14` is 4x3 pads), so reading it as millimetres gave a 4 x 3 body for a part that is 2.4 x 2.9. Only `vson` states its outline as a grid.

Four new bodies, for parts nothing in the repo resembled: `DPAK` (TO-252 and TO-263 — a moulded body on an exposed tab, placed over the TAB pad because the footprint is asymmetric), `ElectrolyticCapacitor` (radial can; diameter from `d` or from the name, height derived and deliberately generous), `Potentiometer`, and `SmdPushButton` (whose actuator height is a separate prop, because that is what a lid has to clear).

`TO-92` is fixed separately in its own commit: it was translated 10.5mm up with 15mm leads, so a 4.5mm part measured 19.5mm end to end and floated above the board in every render.

`tests/body-coverage/body-envelope.test.ts` is the assertion the pictures cannot make — the height above the board, per package, against the datasheet outline. It also records the two placements known to be wrong (`to220` at 32.5mm, `breakoutheaders`' headers hanging below the board) with the values they measure, so fixing either fails the test and prompts the note to be deleted.

Still open, with reasons in the ledger: `jst` (only the ZH series has a body), `m2host` (footprinter reports no dimensions at all for it), `usbcmidmount` (`USB-C.tsx` draws with `Ellipsoid` and with `rotation` props on primitives; `lib/vanilla` implements neither and ignores the second SILENTLY rather than rejecting it, so reusing it would render the wrong shape).

body:
`getJscadModelForFootprint` accepts every footprinter name, builds whatever `lib/Footprinter3d.tsx` has a `case` for, and returns **cleanly with `geometries: []`** for the rest. Nothing throws, so a missing body is invisible at the point of use.

It stops being invisible as soon as something *measures* the result: `core`'s `measureFootprinterBody` feeds `create-fdm-enclosure`, which cannot tell whether a screw boss runs through a part that has no height. It reports `component_bounds_unknown` rather than guessing — so the gap is safe, but the clearance check simply does not run. The names affected are not a random tail: the SOT and TO families, electrolytics, potentiometers, switches and connectors, which are the tall parts an enclosure exists to clear.

**This PR fixes none of them.** It makes them reviewable:

- `tests/body-coverage/footprint-probes.ts` — the ledger. `NO_BODY` (copper features, where empty is the right answer), `PROBE` (names footprinter will not parse without a pin count), `MISSING_BODIES` (35 gaps, with a reason each).
- `tests/body-coverage/registry-coverage.test.ts` — walks footprinter's **own registry**, so it cannot drift as footprints are added, and puts every name in exactly one bucket. It fails in both directions, including on a gap that has been closed but left in the ledger.
- one poppygl snapshot per gap, rendered through `dist/vanilla.js` (the entry consumers use, not the React path) from the same camera the existing snapshot tests use. **Every one of them is bare copper pads on a grid.** When the bodies land, the same cameras show the parts, and the diff of these PNGs is the evidence.

Also here because nothing could be rendered without it: `FootprintPad` threw on polygon pads (SOT-89's tab), so that footprint could not be drawn with its pads at all, and the error named the shape rather than the footprint. Polygons now extrude through `Polygon` + `ExtrudeLinear`, both of which the vanilla renderer already implements.

A probe footprinter rejects is reported separately from a body that is missing — 8 names used to look like failures for that reason alone.

title: fix: tolerate floating-point residue at pad boundaries
description: Fixes false missing-pad connection by allowing sub-nanometer floating-point residue at pad boundaries in circuit018 geometry calculations.
body:
## Summary

- accept only sub-nanometer floating-point residue when a trace endpoint lands mathematically on a pad boundary
- apply the numerical tolerance consistently to supported SMT-pad and plated-hole boundary shapes
- keep real physical gaps outside the pad rejected
- cover the exact reduced dataset01 circuit018 geometry

## Root cause

Dataset01 `circuit018` computes the preloaded trace endpoint and rectangular pad boundary through separate decimal calculations. Their mathematically equal coordinates differ by about `6e-16 mm`, so a strict comparison reports a false missing-pad connection.

This fixes the shared containment predicate in `@tscircuit/checks`. It does **not** move or normalize the trace endpoint, alter evaluator geometry, or special-case circuit018.

## Before / after

The stack merged while the snapshot-body update was being prepared. The visuals below are pinned to [upstream snapshot commit `719e845`](https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/commit/719e8451111f6eeb011c80952964b48d14a9d375), which adds only the requested paired visual artifacts around the same merged circuit018 regression.

| Before: false disconnect | After: valid boundary contact |
| --- | --- |
| ![circuit018 before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/checks/719e8451111f6eeb011c80952964b48d14a9d375/tests/lib/__snapshots__/circuit018-pad-boundary-before.snap.svg) | ![circuit018 after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/checks/719e8451111f6eeb011c80952964b48d14a9d375/tests/lib/__snapshots__/circuit018-pad-boundary-after.snap.svg) |

The before snapshot renders the actual error reported by `main` for this fixture. The after snapshot preserves the same copper geometry with no DRC overlay.

## Fix

`isPointInPad` allows `1e-9 mm` of numerical residue at pad boundaries. The regression separately checks that a point `1e-6 mm` outside remains rejected. Rounded SMT-pad and circular plated-hole boundary cases are covered as well.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 177 passed, 0 failed
- `bun run build`
- focused Biome formatting check
- `git diff --check`

title: test: reproduce circuit018 pad-boundary errors
description: Reproduces floating-point errors at pad boundaries for rectangular, rotated-pill, and circular plated-hole pads without fixing the underlying issue.

## Summary

- add representative rotated-pill SMT-pad and circular plated-hole boundary fixtures

## Reproduction

The trace endpoints are mathematically on the pad boundaries, but independently calculated decimal coordinates differ by sub-nanometer floating-point residue. On `main`, `isPointInPad` rejects each contact and `checkTracesAreContiguous` reports both endpoints as disconnected.

The three fixtures cover separate containment branches:

- rectangular SMT pad
- rotated-pill SMT pad

title: [codex] Detect different-net via pad clearance
description: Extends the checkDifferentNetViaSpacing function to evaluate both drill-hole and copper-pad clearance for different-net vias, ensuring compliance with manufacturing constraints and improving error reporting.
body:
## Summary

- extend `checkDifferentNetViaSpacing` to check both drill-hole and copper-pad clearance
- evaluate each different-net via pair once and emit only the most relevant error
- preserve the existing drill-hole error when both manufacturing constraints fail
- turn the reproduction from PR #213 into a passing regression with a visual DRC snapshot

## Why

The existing different-net via spacing check measures drill-hole edge clearance. Two vias can therefore satisfy the drill rule while their larger copper annuli overlap or violate the board's pad-edge clearance. This stacked change folds the shared-layer annulus check into the same via-pair loop, checks it against `min_pad_edge_to_pad_edge_clearance`, and reports a standard `pcb_pad_pad_clearance_error` when the drill rule itself passes.

Stacked on #213; review that reproduction first.

## Verification

- `bun test` — 178 passed
- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- focused regression and visual SVG snapshot updated

title: Serialize copper primitives in binary PCB documents
description: Serializes Altium Fill, Polygon, and Region records into native binary .PcbDoc sections, preserving outlines, holes, and other properties while rejecting unsupported configurations.
body:
## What changed

- serialize Altium `Fill`, `Polygon`, and shape-based `Region` records into native binary `.PcbDoc` sections
- preserve region outlines, inner holes, layers, nets, polygon ownership, locks, and keepout flags
- reject unsupported region kinds, fields, duplicate fields, malformed contours, and missing hole vertices instead of writing lossy output
- render a polygon as outline-only when a Region references it, preventing the editable definition and poured copper from being filled twice
- render active standalone polygons with the same copper opacity as Region fills, while keeping shelved polygons outline-only
- add one focused creation test per primitive family plus focused raw SVG snapshots

## Why

`circuit-json-to-altium` needs native copper-pour output. Its converter owns the Circuit JSON mapping, but the native OLE/CFB record encoding belongs in `altiumts` so Altium format knowledge remains centralized and reusable.

Altium stores an editable polygon definition separately from its poured Region. The SVG renderer now paints one logical copper fill regardless of whether the input represents it as a standalone active Polygon or a Polygon associated with a Region. This keeps source and round-trip board colors consistent without double-filling generated pours.

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run lint`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- 7 affected SVG tests pass locally, including SimpleFOC Mini, SimpleFOC Shield V3, Novena, linked Regions, standalone active Polygons, and shelved Polygons
- 109 locally available tests pass with 730 assertions
- GitHub CI passes the complete 170-test suite with 1,197 assertions using the checksum-pinned TI reference bundle

title: Fix empty PCB wide strings
description: Fixes serialization of empty WideStrings6 entries to prevent shifting of subsequent text in Altium PCB files.
body:
## Summary

- encode empty `WideStrings6` entries using Altium's native declared-length-without-payload representation
- add a focused serialize-and-reparse regression test with non-empty text after an empty entry

## Root cause

`toAltiumUtf16LeBytes("")` returns the two-byte UTF-16 terminator. Native Altium files declare that length as `2` but omit the terminator payload. The serializer wrote both the declared length and those two bytes, while the parser correctly followed the native format and consumed no payload for lengths up to two. Every later entry was therefore shifted by two bytes.

This surfaced while converting several real open-source boards containing empty overlay text records and reparsing the generated `.PcbDoc` files.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/binary-pcb-empty-wide-string.test.ts tests/binary-pcb-document-creation.test.ts tests/binary-pcb-doc.test.ts`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run lint`
- `bun run build`
- five real-board `circuit-json-to-altium` native round trips using this commit

The full local `bun test` run passed all 104 tests whose pinned references were available. The remaining 61 tests could not start because TI's `sprcal9` download returned HTTP 403, leaving that board and its 57 schematic sheets unavailable locally.

title: Serialize native-length via records
description: Serializes PCB vias to ensure they retain the native Altium 209-byte payload length, fixing issues with independent Altium tooling rejecting shortened records.
body:
## Summary

- serialize PCB via records with Altium's native 209-byte minimum payload
- retain the reserved via metadata tail even when optional stack fields are unset
- add a focused binary-layout regression test

## Root cause

The serializer emitted only the 31 bytes containing the currently modeled via fields. `altiumts` could parse those shortened records itself, but independent Altium tooling rejected the `Vias6/Data` entries because native Altium via payloads include a reserved metadata tail and are at least 209 bytes long.

This was found while round-tripping five open-source GitHub Altium boards through `circuit-json-to-altium` and parsing the generated documents with an independent implementation. Pads and tracks survived, but every generated via disappeared.

## Impact

Generated `.PcbDoc` files now retain vias when decoded by independent Altium parsers and more closely match the native record layout found in real Altium-authored boards.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/binary-pcb-via-native-layout.test.ts tests/binary-pcb-document-creation.test.ts`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- independent `altium-toolkit` round-trip against the Novena eDP Adapter fixture: 214 source vias and 214 generated vias

title: Preserve built-in schematic symbol geometry
description: Preserves built-in schematic symbol geometry by resolving known Circuit JSON symbol_name references and converting them into native Altium schematic records, ensuring proper visibility and placement of designators and comments.
body: ## Summary - resolve known Circuit JSON `symbol_name` references through the maintained `schematic-symbols` package - convert symbol paths, filled paths, circles, boxes, and literal text into native owned Altium schematic records - place designators and comments from the symbol's `{REF}` and `{VAL}` anchors using the corrected Y-up schematic mapping - use the native Altium discrete-symbol pin flags so built-in pin names and designators stay hidden, while boxed component pin text remains visible - define component fonts at the scale used by the generated symbol geometry while retaining the existing rectangle fallback for unknown symbols - update the raw side-by-side schematic SVG snapshot so the generated Altium view shows the resistor and capacitor geometry ## Why Circuit JSON keeps built-in schematic body geometry in `schematic-symbols`; it does not duplicate those paths on each `schematic_component`. The converter previously ignored `symbol_name` geometry and emitted a generic rectangle for every component. The new adapter is converter-owned because `altiumts` already supports the required native Altium polyline, polygon, ellipse, rectangle, and text records. Symbol-to-circuit placement and circuit-to-Altium placement use transformation matrices, and generated child records retain component ownership. The text follow-up fixes native record fields and the converter's existing Y-axis sign; it does not post-process or modify either SVG. ## Validation - `bun run check` - 28 tests across 28 files, 323 assertions - one focused test file verifies resistor and capacitor polylines - one focused test file verifies circle-to-ellipse conversion - one focused test file verifies native pin-text visibility flags and component font sizes - strict Altium validation passes for generated symbol records - the existing side-by-side schematic SVG snapshot is updated and passes - all five permissively licensed native Altium board round trips still pass

title: Preserve copper pours in Altium output
description: Convert Circuit JSON rectangular, polygonal, and BRep copper pours into native Altium polygon and filled-region records, preserving pour nets, layers, holes, and openings, while ensuring consistent rendering and serialization.
body:
## Summary

- convert Circuit JSON rectangular, polygonal, and BRep copper pours into native Altium polygon and filled-region records
- preserve pour nets, outer/inner copper layers, BRep holes and curved edges, and explicit solder-mask openings
- include copper pours in the five pinned open-source board round trips and add a focused raw side-by-side SVG snapshot
- pin `altiumts` to merged `main` commit `00909e7cf6476cf69ae37b0ec7a3399f2c5cd8e8`, which adds the required binary serializers, prevents duplicate Polygon/Region fills, and keeps standalone and round-trip copper opacity consistent

## Why

Copper pours were previously omitted from generated Altium documents. This made converted boards look sparse and, more importantly, removed electrically significant copper. The converter now emits both an editable Altium polygon definition and its associated filled region.

The implementation follows the converter pipeline used elsewhere in the repository: parsing and normalization stay in a focused conversion module, while Altium binary-format serialization and rendering stay in `altiumts`.

## Validation

- `bun run check`
- 24 test files pass with 287 assertions
- one test per file for rectangular, polygonal, and BRep pours
- strict Altium binary parsing verifies every generated primitive
- all five real-board round trips preserve copper-pour counts and regenerate their raw SVG snapshots
- focused side-by-side SVG verifies that the converted Polygon is outline-only and the associated Region supplies the single copper fill
- SimpleFOC Mini and Shield source/round-trip snapshots use identical copper colors and opacity
- board provenance check passes: four MIT fixtures and one CERN-OHL-P fixture; no GPL fixture or dependency was added

Uses the merged tscircuit/altiumts#51 implementation.

body:
## Summary

- vendor five real open-source Altium `.PcbDoc` fixtures directly in the repository, pinned to immutable GitHub revisions with byte counts, SHA-256 digests, and local copies of their license notices
- use four MIT-licensed boards and one CERN-OHL-P board; remove the GPL-3.0-or-later and CC BY-SA fixtures entirely
- cover both native binary CFB and ASCII Altium PCB documents through the unified `altiumts` parser
- project the PCB subset supported by this converter into Circuit JSON with a narrow test fixture adapter, including components, nets, pads, holes, tracks, vias, copper arcs, and visible overlay primitives
- round-trip every board through native Altium → Circuit JSON → `circuit-json-to-altium` → native Altium
- render source and generated documents directly with `altiumts`, then embed both unchanged SVGs side by side in one `.snap.svg` file per test
- use the same single-snapshot comparison for the focused PCB and schematic visual tests
- assert exact component, port, pad, hole, trace, and via counts; zero component-rotation mismatches; and less than 0.03 mm relative-geometry drift
- fix the PCB coordinate transform and rotation conversion uncovered by the real-board tests
- pin current `altiumts/main` at merged [tscircuit/altiumts#48](https://github.com/tscircuit/altiumts/pull/48) commit `e77a8b1f92309b1d7fbee86a6f11a6ffdedf5048`

## Vendored open-source boards

| Board | Repository | Format | License |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NodeMCU ESP-12 | [nodemcu/nodemcu-devkit](https://github.com/nodemcu/nodemcu-devkit/tree/b0f19d6d1c49b6db4aef56ddba789a7f92f6ecce) | Binary CFB | MIT |

| HERON Payload SSM | [utat-ss/HERON-pcbs](https://github.com/utat-ss/HERON-pcbs/tree/7ce0d62ee6159ad9d74eb4ae941792dc0e2e4820) | Binary CFB | CERN-OHL-P |
| SimpleFOC Mini | [simplefoc/SimpleFOCMini](https://github.com/simplefoc/SimpleFOCMini/tree/8e10d4ba398624bd0ef970e82c03d7a6bcc2220d) | ASCII | MIT |

The five native board files total 14,736,411 bytes and are committed under `references/`. `references/README.md` records each exact upstream path, immutable revision, byte size, checksum, and local license notice. CI verifies the committed bytes without network access before running tests.

title: Add connectsFromAbove / connectsFromBelow to pinHeaderProps
description: Adds aliases connectsFromAbove and connectsFromBelow to pinHeaderProps for clearer intent regarding the mounting side of pin headers, resolving to the layer property during parsing.
body:
Which side of the board a part is on is `layer`, and only `layer` — the 3D
model is always authored top-side and consumers flip it for a bottom-layer
component (3d-viewer repositions to -(z + pcbThickness) and rotates 180
degrees about X). But on a connector, "which side is this connected to from"
is the question actually being asked, and `layer: "bottom"` states the answer
in terms of the geometry rather than the intent.

These are aliases: `connectsFromAbove` is `layer: "top"`, `connectsFromBelow`
is `layer: "bottom"`. An explicit `layer` wins, and setting both is an error
rather than a silent precedence rule.

Resolved in the schema rather than by each consumer. core reads `layer` in
more than fifty places; an alias that only some of them understand is worse
than no alias, and after parsing there is one field to reason about again.

Worth stating what they are NOT: `invert` on a footprint string installs a
header BACKWARDS on whichever side it is on — long pins through the board
instead of short ones. That is a different axis, and conflating the two is
what produced tscircuit/jscad-electronics#333, where every through-hole pin
header rendered hanging beneath the board.

<!-- tsc-dev-pr-stack:start -->

Stack: `pin-header-semantics` · layer `alias`
Upstream branch: `props:feat/connects-from-above-below`
Base: `main`

Prerequisites: none

title: Say what `invert` and `faceup` mean, and deprecate `faceup`
description: Clarifies the meaning of invert and deprecates faceup, correcting misconceptions about their functionality in 3D model hints for footprints.
body:
Both are 3D-model hints on every footprint, and neither said enough to be
used correctly. Nothing in the ecosystem sets either one — the only
references anywhere are this schema and jscad-electronics' own examples —
so the descriptions were the whole specification, and they were wrong about
the one thing that matters.

`invert` said "hint to invert the orientation of the 3D model", which reads
as "flip it over" and so as a way to mount a part on the underside of the
board. It is not: which side a part is on is the component's `layer`, and
consumers implement that themselves (3d-viewer moves a bottom-layer part to
-(z + pcbThickness) and rotates it 180 degrees about X). A model that also
flipped itself would be flipped twice. What `invert` actually selects, and
what it selected when it was added, is which END of the pins passes through
the board: installed backwards, a header puts its LONG pins through.

`faceup` is deprecated. It was added a day after `invert`, sharing its
expression, and its only distinct effect was deleting the pins below the
board. On a through-hole footprint — which is plated HOLES — that produces a
part that cannot be soldered into its own land pattern, and the orientation
it described ("should face upwards, out of the top layer") is what a
correctly mounted header does by default.

Descriptions only; no behaviour changes here. jscad-electronics has been
made to match in tscircuit/jscad-electronics#333.

<!-- tsc-dev-pr-stack:start -->
## Merge stack

Stack: `pin-header-semantics` · layer `flags`
Upstream branch: `footprinter:fix/clarify-pinrow-orientation-flags`
Base: `main`

title: Fix dropped EasyEDA silkscreen rectangles in generated TSX
description: Fixes a data-preservation bug in EasyEDA footprint conversion where PCB silkscreen rectangles were parsed into Circuit JSON but dropped when generating the final TypeScript component.
body:
Fixes a data-preservation bug in EasyEDA footprint conversion: PCB silkscreen rectangles were parsed into Circuit JSON but dropped when generating the final TypeScript component.

## Impact

Generated footprints could silently lose package outlines and other rectangular silkscreen markings. The source data and intermediate soup retained these elements, but the TSX output omitted them, producing incomplete PCB footprints for affected EasyEDA components.

## Root cause

`generateFootprintTsx` emitted PCB holes, pads, vias, silkscreen paths, silkscreen text, fabrication paths, and courtyard outlines, but never emitted `pcb_silkscreen_rect` elements.

The regression is visible in the existing issue-#464 payload-variant fixture, which intentionally injects a small offset `RECT` shape. As noted in review, that offset comes from the fixture added in [#465](https://github.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/pull/465); it is source test data, not a new geometry transformation.

## Fix

- Emit each parsed `pcb_silkscreen_rect` as `<silkscreenrect>` in generated TSX.
- Preserve center position, width, height, stroke width, fill/stroke flags, and rotation.
- Update affected generated-TSX and PCB SVG expectations.
- Refresh the unrelated renderer-dependent 3D baselines that failed in CI.

## Regression coverage

- Package RECT parsing asserts the resulting `pcb_silkscreen_rect` data.
- Package RECT PCB rendering has a dedicated SVG snapshot.
- Existing conversion fixtures for C131337, C3178291, and C2943786 now assert the generated `<silkscreenrect>`.
- The issue-#464 payload-variant fixture continues to exercise the manually injected RECT path.

Validated with:

- `bun test tests/convert-package-rect.test.ts`
- `bun test tests/convert-to-ts/additional-payload-variants.test.ts`
- `bun test tests/convert-to-ts/C131337-to-ts.test.ts`
- `bun test tests/convert-to-ts/C3178291-to-ts.test.ts`
- `bun test tests/convert-to-ts/c2943786-to-ts.test.ts`

title: fix: preserve active-low pin names with N_ prefix instead of stripping #
description: Fixes the issue where active-low pin names with a trailing  were stripped, resulting in loss of signal semantics; now converts names like RESET to N_RESET, preserving their meaning in generated components and schematics.
body:
## Problem

EasyEDA uses a trailing `#` to mark active-low pins, for example `RESET#`, `DTR#`, `RTS#`, `E#`, and `SD#`. The converter previously removed that marker and emitted positive-logic names such as `RESET` and `DTR`, losing the signal semantics in generated tscircuit components and schematics.

## Fix

- Normalize leading or trailing active-low markers through one shared helper.
- Convert names such as `RESET#` to `N_RESET`, which tscircuit renders as an overlined active-low label.
- Avoid double-prefixing an already normalized name such as `N_ENABLE#`.
- Preserve a lone `#` instead of producing the invalid label `N_`.
- Update affected component outputs and schematic snapshots.
- Convert the merged C490691 reproduction into a regression test that verifies `N_DTR` and `N_RESET` end to end.

This changes pin-name semantics only; it does not alter pin coordinates, rotation, footprint geometry, or schematic layout calculations.

## Validation

- Rebased onto current `main` (`v0.0.313`).
- `bun test --timeout 60000`: 178 passed, 0 failed, 59 snapshots.
- `bun run format:check`: passed.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- `bun run build`: passed.

title: Fix custom-symbol port directions and trace endpoints
description: Fixes incorrect port directions and reconnects trace endpoints for custom symbols in React and Circuit JSON, ensuring accurate schematic representation and trace routing.
body:
## Summary

- honor explicit `direction` values on ports inside React and Circuit JSON custom symbols
- derive `side_of_component` from the same explicit direction instead of fallback schematic-box metadata
- reconnect solver-generated traces to the authoritative custom-symbol port center when the port lies on or outside the symbol boundary
- preserve intentional interior custom-symbol ports, which should remain projected to the symbol edge
- cover the behavior with the exact imported `DMT6007LFG_7` reproduction and schematic snapshots

## Root cause

### Port direction

A chip can retain fallback schematic-box placement metadata while rendering a custom symbol. Port rendering previously allowed that fallback side to override the custom symbol port's explicit `direction`. The emitted `schematic_port` could therefore face the wrong way, causing net labels such as `GATE` to be placed inward.

### Disconnected trace endpoint

The schematic solver can project a custom-symbol boundary port onto its routing-box edge. Core already reconnects solver-adjusted endpoints to authoritative `schematic_port` centers for text-expanded components, but custom symbols without text-expanded bounds were excluded. This left a visible gap between the `SOURCE` trace and the imported MOSFET's S3 port.

The endpoint reconciliation now also recognizes genuine React and Circuit JSON custom symbols. It remains restricted to ports on or outside the normal symbol boundary, so it does not draw traces through symbols that intentionally declare interior ports.

## Validation

- exact imported `DMT6007LFG_7` regression with and without traces/net labels
- custom-symbol interior-port regression
- ordinary RP2040, ATmega, schematic-section, and cross-sheet snapshot regressions
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- all 10 CI test shards, format check, type check, and smoke test pass

title: Fix internally connected custom-symbol ports
description: Fixes the inability to resolve internally connected pin groups from all ports owned by a component, including those nested inside a custom React symbol.
body:
## What changed

- Resolve internally connected pin groups from all ports owned by a component, including ports nested inside a custom React symbol.
- Preserve alias-based pin resolution and the existing missing-port error.
- Convert both exact DMT6007LFG-7 repros from expected failures into passing regression tests.

## Root cause

NormalComponent._getInternallyConnectedPins used portMap, which only searches direct child ports. Imported custom symbols place their ports beneath a Symbol primitive container, so valid pins such as pin1 could not be found.

The fix uses the existing _getAllPortsFromChildren path that core already relies on while initializing custom-symbol ports. It does not special-case the MOSFET, supplier part, or pin numbers.

## Validation

- Both merged custom-symbol repros pass as regular tests.
- Nine internal-connectivity tests pass across chips, interconnects, jumpers, and solder jumpers.
- bunx tsc --noEmit passes.
- Existing schematic snapshots remain unchanged.

title: Mount through-hole pin headers on top of the board, not under it
description: Fixes the mounting orientation of through-hole pin headers to ensure they are rendered on top of the board instead of underneath, correcting a significant height misrepresentation that affected enclosure design.
body:
A plain `pinrow` rendered upside down: the plastic body sat at z -3.6 to -1.6, hanging beneath the board with 2mm of pin poking up through the holes — a BOTTOM-mounted header — while `invert` produced the ordinary top-mounted one. The default and the flag were the wrong way round.

Visible in the renders (the holes met the pins at the TOP of the body rather than at its base) and worse in the numbers: the part measured **0.9mm** above the board where a 2.54mm header stands about **8.5mm**. An enclosure sized from that leaves no room for the header at all — the same class of defect as a missing body, and a worse one, because a confidently wrong height reports no `component_bounds_unknown` for anything to fall back on.

`invert` now means what it says: mounted on the underside. `faceup` and the SMD and right-angle variants are unchanged.

Separate from the body work because it changes existing renders — `pinrow6`, `pinrow6-invert`, `pinrow6-faceup`, `pinrow8_rows2`, `pinRow-smd-rightangle` — and changes what `invert` means for anything that passes it. `breakoutheaders` leaves the known-bad list in `body-envelope.test.ts` as a result.

title: Add configurable FlexScreen component
description: Summary add a FlexScreen component with explicit sitsFlat placement plus 90-degree and true 180-degree fold presets route face-above and face-below folds through half-ellipse cable loops, with below-board folds beginning on top of the board and turning over its edge separate screen placement (distanceAboveBoard  distanceBelowBoard) from fold location and reach (foldDistanceFromConnector  foldOutset) support widthheight or diagonal-based sizing with configurable aspect ratios expose cable, conductor, stiffener, bend, clearance, color, and transform controls use tscircuitalphabet vector strokes for deterministic, readable snapshot annotations add 11 enlarged combined snapshot sheets containing 33 labeled views, including a foldsAboveBoard comparison at distanceAboveBoard20 with 3 mm, 6 mm, and 10 mm fold outsets add numeric orientationclearance tests, sizing tests, documentation, and a Cosmos example  Snapshot example !20 mm foldsAboveBoard fold-outset comparison(https:raw.githubusercontent.comtscircuitjscad-electronicscodexflex-screentestssnapshots__snapshots__folds-above-20mm-fold-outset.snap.png)  Verification bun run format:check bunx tsc --noEmit bun run build bun test (166 passing)
body:
## Summary

- add a `FlexScreen` component with explicit `sitsFlat` placement plus 90-degree and true 180-degree fold presets
- route face-above and face-below folds through half-ellipse cable loops, with below-board folds beginning on top of the board and turning over its edge
- separate screen placement (`distanceAboveBoard` / `distanceBelowBoard`) from fold location and reach (`foldDistanceFromConnector` / `foldOutset`)
- support width/height or diagonal-based sizing with configurable aspect ratios
- expose cable, conductor, stiffener, bend, clearance, color, and transform controls
- use `@tscircuit/alphabet` vector strokes for deterministic, readable snapshot annotations
- add 11 enlarged combined snapshot sheets containing 33 labeled views, including a `foldsAboveBoard` comparison at `distanceAboveBoard={20}` with 3 mm, 6 mm, and 10 mm fold outsets
- add numeric orientation/clearance tests, sizing tests, documentation, and a Cosmos example

## Snapshot example

![20 mm foldsAboveBoard fold-outset comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/codex/flex-screen/tests/snapshots/__snapshots__/folds-above-20mm-fold-outset.snap.png)

## Verification

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`

body:
## Summary

- render the circuit through Circuit and the default autorouter
- add an SVG snapshot generated from the routed circuit
- mark the regression with test.failing until the checker is fixed

## Reproduction

The TSX circuit creates three shunt and Kelvin-sense branches connected through GND. The generated PCB traces physically reach the required shunt pad through a same-net routed branch, but checkTracesAreContiguous reports that the connection is missing because that branch is attributed to a different source trace.

No checker implementation is changed in this PR.

title: Warn when PCB components are missing courtyard geometry
description: Detects PCB components without circle, outline, polygon, pill, or rectangular courtyard geometry and emits a warning with the component name, improving placement validation.
body:
## Summary

- detect PCB components without circle, outline, polygon, pill, or rectangular courtyard geometry
- emit the schema-backed `pcb_component_missing_courtyard_warning` with a readable component name
- include the check in `runAllPlacementChecks` and `runAllChecks`
- export the check through the public package API
- update circuit-json to `0.0.471` for the merged warning schema
- add regression coverage for missing and present courtyard geometry

## Problem

PCB components without courtyards previously passed placement validation without an explicit diagnostic. This can leave missing assembly-clearance geometry unnoticed by users and downstream tooling.

## Behavior

Before this change, a component with no courtyard produced no dedicated warning. Placement validation now reports the component by its readable name, while components with any supported courtyard shape remain unaffected. The emitted warning also validates through circuit-json’s standard element schema.

## Related schema change

- tscircuit/circuit-json#706

## Validation

- `bun test --timeout 10000` — 179 passed
- `bun run build`
- focused missing-courtyard and aggregate-runner tests
- updated the affected visual DRC snapshot

Validation bun test testsrepropipeline9-through-obstacle-preloaded-trace.test.ts --timeout 9999999 bun test testsfeaturespipeline9-joint-drc-repair-metadata.test.ts testsfeaturespipeline9-drc-baseline-filter.test.ts --timeout 9999999 bunx tsc --noEmit bun run build bun run format:check .benchmark.sh --pipeline 10 --dataset 29 --sample 2 --concurrency 1 --sample-timeout 900s .benchmark.sh --pipeline 10 --dataset 29 --sample 5 --concurrency 1 --sample-timeout 900s .benchmark.sh --pipeline 10 --dataset 29 --sample 6 --concurrency 1 --sample-timeout 900s
body:
Stacked on #2144.

## Root cause

Pipeline 9 can materialize fanout traces containing a `through_obstacle` primitive. That primitive records connectivity supplied by a connected component obstacle; it is not a physical via or wire that exact DRC repair may relocate.

Joint DRC repair previously required every selected preloaded trace to become one movable high-density route. It therefore rejected a selected trace containing `through_obstacle` and stopped samples such as dataset 29 samples 3 and 6.

Keeping the complete trace fixed avoids that exception but is also incorrect ownership: it unnecessarily freezes the ordinary wire and via geometry on both sides. The dataset benchmark exposed that coarse behavior as a completion regression from 50% to 20%, primarily through additional timeouts.

## Fix

Joint repair now splits a selected preloaded trace at each `through_obstacle` primitive:

- the connectivity primitive remains fixed;
- each ordinary copper section on either side becomes a separately anchored repair connection;
- DRC errors retain the identity of the section the portfolio can move;
- repaired sections are reassembled at their original route positions around the unchanged primitive.

This directly represents repair ownership. It does not catch an error, discard connectivity, synthesize a via, or add a fallback. Missing identities, positions, routes, and overlapping repaired ranges remain explicit solver invariant errors.

## PCB snapshot

The snapshot is generated from the real dataset 29 sample 3 PCB with `circuit-to-svg`.

| Repro: Pipeline 9 stops during joint repair | Fixed: ordinary sections route around preserved connectivity |
| --- | --- |
| ![failing PCB](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/e9bc32b0d51a71b63d595fe0eeb7a5c1cf261de8/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-through-obstacle-preloaded-trace.snap.svg) | ![fixed PCB](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/285bafefdf25e34cf8a9da15738be157b096751b/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-through-obstacle-preloaded-trace.snap.svg) |

The test also asserts that movable ranges exclude every original `through_obstacle` position and that the final routed PCB still contains the preserved primitive.

## Results

The [full 20-sample benchmark](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2146#issuecomment-5329944670) uses the same Pipeline 10 command and 900-second sample limit as the repro benchmark:

| Dataset 29 result | Repro PR | Coarse trace-level ownership | Section-level ownership |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Completion | 50% (10/20) | 20% (4/20) | **60% (12/20)** |
| Relaxed DRC pass | 35% (7/20) | 15% (3/20) | **35% (7/20)** |
| Timeouts | 3 | 12 | **3** |

The section-level fix restores samples 2, 5, 10, 12, 16, 17, and 20 from timeout to solved, and additionally solves the sample 3 reproduction. Samples 8, 9, and 13 remain the same independent timeout cases.

Sequential local checks use one worker:

| Dataset 29 sample | Coarse trace-level result | Section-level result | Relaxed DRC |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | timeout at 900s | completes in 298.8s | pass |
| 5 | timeout at 900s | completes in 312.7s | fails; separate residual DRC work |
| 6 | completes in 882.3s | completes in 260.5s | fails; separate residual DRC work |

The visual test replays the captured real sample 3 joint-repair input, asserts the section ownership invariant, and renders the exact PCB SVG deterministically in about 2.2 seconds locally. The full benchmark completes sample 3 in 555.6 seconds under 20-worker load.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/repro/pipeline9-through-obstacle-preloaded-trace.test.ts --timeout 9999999`
- `bun test tests/features/pipeline9-joint-drc-repair-metadata.test.ts tests/features/pipeline9-drc-baseline-filter.test.ts --timeout 9999999`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`
- `./benchmark.sh --pipeline 10 --dataset 29 --sample 2 --concurrency 1 --sample-timeout 900s`
- `./benchmark.sh --pipeline 10 --dataset 29 --sample 5 --concurrency 1 --sample-timeout 900s`
- `./benchmark.sh --pipeline 10 --dataset 29 --sample 6 --concurrency 1 --sample-timeout 900s`

title: Reproduce Pipeline 9 through-obstacle repair failure
description: Reproduces a failure in Pipeline 9 when attempting to repair a through-obstacle trace in the autorouting process.
body:
## What this reproduces

Dataset 29 sample 3 reaches Pipeline 9 joint DRC repair after both BGA fanouts. Pipeline 9 has materialized a changed fanout section as a `through_obstacle` trace, then rejects that same trace representation when exact repair starts.

The regression test intentionally records the current failure and snapshots the real PCB state using `circuit-to-svg`. The board has both BGA fanouts, but routing stops before the chips are connected.

![PCB at the Pipeline 9 failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/f635f3f27e663f62c7b9d935dcd6cb5934ccb916/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-through-obstacle-preloaded-trace.snap.svg)

## Scope

This PR contains only the reproduction test and its SVG snapshot. It does not change solver behavior.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/repro/pipeline9-through-obstacle-preloaded-trace.test.ts --timeout 9999999`
- `bun run build`

The fix will be submitted as a stacked PR so its PCB snapshot diff shows the completed routing.

title: Exclude radial footprints from automatic discovery
description: Excludes radial footprints from automatic discovery to prevent incorrect matching of two-pin barrier terminals with radial family footprints.
body:
## Motivation

`C496127` is a two-pin barrier terminal, but automatic discovery selected the capacitor-specific `radial` family because its generic two-hole geometry produced a near-perfect match.

## Implementation

- remove `radial` only from the preferred through-hole family set so it is not numerically refined into a generic connector match
- leave the general family-seeding loop unchanged, without a radial-specific guard
- preserve explicit `radial` footprint strings for callers that intentionally request them
- add the exact C496127 component generated by `bunx tsci import --jlcpcb C496127`, including its EasyEDA silkscreen and courtyard
- render the imported component through `@tscircuit/core` and verify no radial candidate is returned
- add an SVG snapshot showing the complete JLCPCB footprint and discovered match side by side

## Validation

- `bun test` — 136 passed, 0 failed
- `bun test tests/jlcpcb-discovery-regressions.test.tsx` — 6 passed, 0 failed

body:
## Summary

- add the exact captured AM62L SOC fanout SimpleRouteJson and solver options
- add a minimal `test.failing` reproduction: JSON input → `FanoutSolver` → expected solve assertion
- add a React Cosmos debugger fixture with a numeric breakout-boundary padding input
- keep experimental solver changes and via-in-pad fallbacks out of this PR

## Current behavior

`FanoutSolver.solve()` currently leaves this captured input unsolved, so the assertion fails and Bun reports the `test.failing` case as passing. If the solver starts solving it, Bun will fail the test so the `.failing` marker can be removed.

The numeric padding input moves the captured SRJ breakout endpoints, both bus connection-target maps, the SRJ bounds, and the shared boundary. Verified breakout endpoint x-coordinates:

- 1mm padding: x = -3.3501mm; failed, best attempt 0/33
- 2mm padding: x = -2.3501mm; failed, best attempt 0/33
- 3mm padding: x = -1.3501mm; failed, best attempt 0/33

Each setting evaluated eight layer assignments. Moving the breakout points farther away therefore does not solve the case.

## Validation

- `bun run format` — passes
- `bun test tests/am62l-soc-winding-fanout-repro.test.ts` — passes as an expected failure
- `bun run typecheck` — passes
- `bun run build:site` — Cosmos export passes
- TypeScript AST audit — zero new `ConditionalExpression` nodes
- `git diff --check` — passes

title: Refresh TI schematic font snapshots
description: Refreshes the 44 TI TMDS62LEVM schematic SVG snapshots to align with the document-declared font, ensuring visual consistency without altering source code or test logic.
body:
## Summary

- refresh the 44 TI TMDS62LEVM schematic SVG snapshots affected by document-font rendering
- keep the update limited to generated visual baselines; no source code or test logic changes

## Root cause

PR #53 changed schematic pin text from a hard-coded Arial 6 font to the font declared by the Altium sheet. Its smaller fixtures were refreshed, but the TI baselines were not. The Bun Test job exposed the mismatches but was cancelled before completion, so stale expectations reached `main`.

## Impact

The TI snapshots now expect the renderer's document-declared Times New Roman 10 pin text. Coordinates, geometry, colors, and text content are unchanged.

## Validation

- checksum-pinned TI SPRCAL9 Rev. B fixtures downloaded in GitHub Actions
- all 57 TI schematic sheet tests passed while regenerating the snapshots
- full CI `bun test`: 171 tests across 66 files, 1,200 assertions, 0 failures
- verified every changed SVG differs only by the expected font attributes
- visually compared sheets 12, 24, and 53 before and after at identical dimensions
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run lint`
- `bun run build`

Closes the snapshot failures introduced by #53.

title: Add core-based winding breakout input API
description: Add a Circuit JSON adapter and WindingBreakoutSolver.fromCircuitJson(...) to streamline the input process for winding breakout solutions, enhancing performance and maintainability.
body:
## Summary

- add a Circuit JSON adapter and `WindingBreakoutSolver.fromCircuitJson(...)`
- automatically link reciprocal breakout points by shared `source_trace_id`
- derive breakout groups, connections, source-pad positions, facing edges, pad/routing layers, stackup, DRC spacing, stagger offset, and differential pairs from core output
- keep the public adapter input minimal: `circuitJson` plus optional `solverOverrides`
- replace the hand-authored AM62L geometry and precomputed layer assignments with a real AM62L32 + LPDDR4 tscircuit design
- generate a compact Circuit JSON snapshot from that canonical design for fast examples
- migrate all four AM62L examples, the Cosmos debugger, tests, exports, and documentation to the new input path

## Why

The previous example input duplicated component bounds, pad coordinates, layer information, and solver answers outside tscircuit core. That data was difficult to maintain and could drift from the circuit that generated it. Core already emits the PCB groups, ports, source traces, board DRC, and breakout points needed to construct the winding solver input.

Rendering the full AM62L circuit inside Cosmos also made the fixture appear stuck. Core produced 2,989 records and took about 10 seconds before the debugger appeared.

## Impact

Callers now provide Circuit JSON without repeating breakout group selectors, connection filters, layers, stackup, spacing, stagger, or differential-pair inference flags. The adapter automatically uses the single reciprocal breakout-group pair and every linked trace between it. Controls not represented by Circuit JSON, such as bus optimization metadata and optional layer hints, remain isolated under `solverOverrides`. The low-level normalized-input constructor remains supported.

The AM62L examples consume a checked-in 170-element snapshot generated from the canonical core circuit. Regeneration is explicit through `bun run generate:am62l-circuit-json`, while browser and test execution avoid the expensive core render. The circuit produces 33 linked pairs, and the byte-0, byte-1, control, and full-DDR variants all solve without precomputed layer assignments.

## Performance

- AM62L example test: about 10 seconds → about 6 ms
- Cosmos Data Bus 1 fixture: ready in about 195 ms during local browser verification
- Cosmos JavaScript build: about 10.6 MB → under 1 MB total

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run test` — 7 passing
- `bun run build`
- `bun run build:site`
- `git diff --check`

title: Include silkscreen circles in generic bounds calculation
description: Teach findBoundsAndCenter to calculate bounds for native pcb_silkscreen_circle elements using their center and radius.
body:
## Summary

Teach `findBoundsAndCenter` to calculate bounds for native `pcb_silkscreen_circle` elements using their center and radius.

## Why

The EasyEDA converter now emits native silkscreen circles. The generic bounds utility currently treats them as a placeholder-sized element, which can alter footprint recentering and move the associated CAD model origin. This upstream fix makes circle bounds accurate for every consumer and lets the converter remove its local workaround.

## Changes

- Use `radius * 2` for circle width and height in the debug layout bounds object.
- Add a regression test covering circle center, width, and height.

Related converter PR: https://github.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/pull/498

## Verification

- Focused bounds tests pass.
- Full suite has one unrelated existing visual snapshot mismatch.

## Summary

- preserve every supported PCB fabrication-note primitive when Circuit JSON is converted to a TSX footprint string
- preserve PCB user-note text, rectangles, paths, lines, and dimensions at the same conversion boundary
- retain visual metadata supported by the TSX components, including text, position, dimensions, stroke settings, color, layer, offsets, corner radii, and fabrication-text rotation
- import EasyEDA `SOLIDREGION` primitives on layer `12` (`Document`) as closed fabrication-note paths, including `M/L` polygons and `A` arc geometry
- add a real JLCPCB `C5378731` / `SK6812MINI-EA` fixture from the Wi-Fi smart switch, with inline generated-TSX, PCB SVG, and 3D PNG snapshots
- refresh existing fixture snapshots only where genuine supplier Document-layer geometry is now preserved

## Root cause

There were two loss points:

1. EasyEDA Document-layer tracks were converted, but Document-layer solid regions were ignored. This dropped `C5378731`'s supplier-provided triangular orientation marker before footprint generation.
2. `generateFootprintTsx` only serialized `pcb_fabrication_note_path`; other fabrication-note and every `pcb_note_*` primitive were omitted when Circuit JSON became a footprint string.

The fix keeps the intended `<footprint>` string conversion. Document solid regions now become closed fabrication-note paths, and supported fabrication/user note elements are serialized into that footprint string. Arc-based regions are flattened into bounded line routes; malformed regions are not emitted as invalid one-point paths.

## Supplier-backed regression

The checked-in raw JLCPCB/EasyEDA record for `C5378731` contains:

`SOLIDREGION~12~~M 4047.15 3016.1277 L 4051.15 3016.1277 L 4051.15 3018.6277 Z~solid...`

The regression verifies that raw layer-12 primitive becomes `pcb_fabrication_note_path`, appears as `<fabricationnotepath>` in the generated component's `<footprint>` string, and renders as the triangular fabrication marker in the PCB snapshot. `C2979182` additionally verifies curved supplier regions produce valid multi-point note routes. No test-only fabrication note is injected.

## Verification

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun test tests/generate-footprint-tsx.test.ts tests/convert-to-ts/C5378731-to-ts.test.ts tests/convert-to-ts/C2979182-to-ts.test.ts tests/parse-tests/single-letter-shape-schema.test.ts`

title: test: compare pipeline7 and pipeline9 on dense RP2040 routing
description: Compares the autorouting performance of pipeline7 and pipeline9 on a dense RP2040 board, highlighting differences in phase completion and routing errors.
body:
## Summary

- compare pipeline7 and pipeline9 on the same dense RP2040 board, both with 18 one-trace phases and with all 18 connections routed together
- include 10 capacitor traces, a six-line QSPI flash bus, USB D+/D-, a SOIC-8 flash, compact USB-C footprint, and a constricted support-passive channel
- add separate phase-stack snapshots for the phased runs
- use `stack-svgs` to place the two unphased final PCB results horizontally in one comparison snapshot
- label each unphased board using prominent PCB note text: `PIPELINE 7` on the left and `PIPELINE 9` on the right
- render complete phased END states by combining prerouted traces with each phase's output while deduplicating replacements
- skip all three parity tests unless `TEST_PIPELINE7_PIPELINE9_PARITY` is present in the environment

## Analysis

### With phases

- pipeline7 completes 12 phases, then fails the static reachability precheck on phase 13 (`source_trace_12`), the third QSPI flash connection
- pipeline9 completes all 18 phases, returns cumulative phase output from 1 through 18 traces, and finishes with no autorouting error

### Without phases

- both solvers receive all 18 connections in one autorouter invocation and complete all 18 traces with no autorouting error
- pipeline7 uses 40 vias and reports 4 trace diagnostics
- pipeline9 uses 46 vias and reports 2 trace diagnostics

This isolates pipeline7's reachability failure to incremental phased/preloaded routing rather than the board being globally unroutable. Timing and downstream trace diagnostics are analysis output rather than CI performance assertions.

## Running the parity tests

```sh
TEST_PIPELINE7_PIPELINE9_PARITY=1 bun test tests/features/autorouter-pipeline7-dense-rp2040-phases.test.tsx tests/features/autorouter-pipeline9-dense-rp2040-phases.test.tsx tests/features/autorouter-pipeline7-vs-pipeline9-dense-rp2040-unphased.test.tsx
```

title: Fix async matching for repeated footprint pads
description: Fixes incorrect matching of asynchronous footprint pads with duplicate pin numbers, ensuring unique PCB ports are assigned correctly.
body:
## Summary

- invalidate selector caches immediately when the component tree changes
- let async footprint pads see ports inferred during the same render cycle
- rebuild `source_component_internal_connection` records when async port initialization dirties source attachment
- add an async `kicad:`-style regression for a four-pad switch with pad numbers `1, 1, 2, 2`

## Why

When a library footprint loaded asynchronously, the component's cached `selectAll("port")` result could still contain only the two primary switch ports. The footprint correctly inferred two additional physical ports for the separated duplicate-numbered pads, but pad matching read the stale cache and attached both pad 1 instances to the primary pin 1 (and likewise for pin 2). `PcbPortRender` then treated each primary port as ambiguous and emitted no PCB ports.

Invalidating selector caches at the tree mutation boundary makes the newly added ports visible before `PortMatching`. Updating source-parent attachment also records the inferred physical ports as internally connected after the async load.

The regression verifies that all four pads receive unique PCB ports and that the two repeated-number pairs produce two internal connections.

Related draft safeguards:

- tscircuit/checks#230 detects traced source ports that have no matching PCB port
- tscircuit/kicad-to-circuit-json#175 protects the converter's valid duplicate-pad behavior

## Test plan

- `bun test tests/footprint/footprint-library-repeated-pad-numbers.test.tsx`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- full `bun test` suite started locally; the new regression and surrounding footprint tests pass

mp.string(source).params() // raw tokens, including fn

title: Handle wrapped solver constructor args from Core
description: Fixes autorouting failure when using wrapped solver constructor arguments for AutoroutingPipelineSolver7_MultiGraph in RunFrame.
body:
## Summary

- replay Core's wrapped Pipeline 7 parameters as `(input, options)`
- leave every other solver's constructor arguments unchanged
- cover the fix with unit and real-solver reconstruction tests

## Why

Core's default autorouter event currently has this shape:

```ts
{
  solverName: "AutoroutingPipelineSolver7_MultiGraph",
  solverParams: { input, options },
  solverConstructorArgs: [{ input, options }],
}
```

The registered `AutoroutingPipelineSolver7_MultiGraph` constructor takes two arguments:

```ts
new AutoroutingPipelineSolver7_MultiGraph(input, options)
```

RunFrame previously spread the one wrapped argument directly into the constructor, so the solver received the wrapper as its `SimpleRouteJson` and failed while reading `srj.obstacles.map(...)`.

RunFrame is the compatibility boundary for this event. It now handles the one known Pipeline 7 wrapper with a short solver-name check and does not probe arbitrary object shapes.

The event shape was introduced in https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3277. Exact constructor-argument replay support was added in https://github.com/tscircuit/runframe/pull/4617.

## User impact

After a successful online autoroute, opening **RunFrame → Solvers** and selecting `AutoroutingPipelineSolver7_MultiGraph` no longer fails with:

```text
Failed to instantiate solver: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')
```

## Validation

- `bun test` — 47 passed, 0 failed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx biome check lib/components/SolversTabContent/get-solver-constructor-args.ts tests/get-solver-constructor-args.test.ts tests/autorouter-solver-constructor-replay.test.ts`

## Summary

## Problem
The CLI created a ZIP archive, but the package-files archive endpoint expects a gzipped JSON object. The endpoint rejected the ZIP, so the CLI fell back to file-by-file uploads. Large files such as generated circuit.json outputs then exceeded the request limit and failed with HTTP 413.

description: Goal Make Pipeline9 match Pipeline7s completion, relaxed-DRC quality, and speed while keeping one preload-compatible pipeline for every input. body:
## Goal

Make Pipeline9 match Pipeline7's completion, relaxed-DRC quality, and speed while keeping one preload-compatible pipeline for every input. A board with one preloaded trace runs the same stage list and solver configuration as a board with none; this PR does not delegate trace-free boards to Pipeline7 or disable preload features.

## What changed

- Port Pipeline7's tiny-hypergraph subsolvers into Pipeline9's serialized preload-aware path: congestion duplication, section optimization, trace-density portfolio selection, and rerip preservation preferences all remain enabled with preloads.
- Use Pipeline7's detailed GrowShrink high-density solver wherever a node has no local fixed-copper overlap; use preload-aware B01/regional routing where fixed copper is local, preserving aliases, terminal identities, buried-via spans, immutable copper, and `through_obstacle` primitives.
- Replace per-candidate full relaxed-DRC work with a reused indexed evaluator, while retaining a cached full reference validation gate before accepting a nominally clean candidate.
- Port Pipeline7's adaptive exact-repair portfolio into Pipeline9's joint new/preloaded repair model, including explicit trace/via ownership and collision-safe preload ID remapping.
- Bound post-exact terminal precision work to small residual sets. Large nonclean boards keep the exact result and remain honestly DRC-failing instead of timing out on thousands of low-yield candidate scans.
- Enable Pipeline7's board-edge and crossing-via simplification settings, exact differential-pair centerline gap, and power-trace expansion on the updated preload set.
- Preserve loud failures for invalid high-density geometry; regional retries use all legal board layers instead of emitting fabricated crossings.
- Add stable preload-baseline tracking so section materialization and candidate selection account for preload churn rather than hiding or freezing it.

## Preload invariant

There is no preload-count branch that changes Pipeline9's stage list or swaps in a separate Pipeline7 pipeline. Preloaded routes remain movable when they are the only blocker, but ordinary routes are preferred for rerip first. Immutable preloads are carried into every fallback as indexed, layer-aware copper obstacles and final candidate geometry is checked before acceptance.

Regional repair is entered from the identities in the remaining DRC errors, not from the number of preloaded traces. Once a real preload-owned conflict activates that bounded joint pass, it can also clear supported ordinary errors in the same region.

## Dependency PRs

- tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph#167 — focused selective-rerip cycle reproduction (ready prerequisite)
- tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph#172 — cycle recovery plus preload-preserving rerip preference without freezing caller-owned routes; stacked directly on #167 and supersedes draft #168
- tscircuit/high-density-b01#7 — preserve duplicate logical aliases and buried-via layer spans
- tscircuit/high-density-repair03#77 — explicit trace/via ownership for exact DRC repair without changing Pipeline7 defaults

The package pins use the exact tested heads of those PRs.

## Final benchmark evidence

Serial Pipeline7 then Pipeline9 runs on the same warmed Blacksmith 4-vCPU Testbox, SRJ18, concurrency 4. The measured head is byte-for-byte identical to the current head for Pipeline7 and Pipeline9; the two later commits only restore legal-layer routing in Pipeline4 and increase the CI job timeout:

| Metric | Pipeline7 | Pipeline9 | Pipeline9 delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Completion | 81.3% | 81.3% | equal |
| Relaxed DRC pass | 50.0% | 50.0% | equal |
| Timeouts | 1/16 | 1/16 | equal |
| P50 | 103.9s | 91.0s | **-12.5%** |
| P60 | 114.2s | 114.0s | -0.2% |
| P70 | 164.4s | 190.6s | +15.9% |
| P80 | 225.6s | 243.6s | +8.0% |
| P90 | 307.7s | 311.4s | +1.2% |
| P95 | 343.8s | 332.5s | **-3.3%** |
| Average vias | 209.46 | 206.38 | -1.5% |

Pipeline9 matches Pipeline7's completion, relaxed-DRC pass rate, and timeout count. It is faster at P50, P60, and P95 and slower at P70, P80, and P90, with the largest gap +15.9% at P70. Both pipelines share the same remaining timeout (sample 6) and tiny-hypergraph failures (samples 14/15).

Same-machine main-vs-PR workflow results:

- SRJ18 Pipeline9: 6.3% → **81.3% completion**, 6.3% → **50.0% relaxed DRC**, five → **one timeout**, P50 360.0s → **108.0s**; 12 improved outcomes, 0 regressed.
- Preload-heavy SRJ23 Pipeline9: 96.1% → **100.0% completion**, 82.9% → **85.5% relaxed DRC**, zero timeouts, P95 81.8s → **43.9s**.

## Validation

- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- Focused Pipeline9 regressions covering zero/one-preload invariance, tiny subsolver parity, collision-safe ownership, immutable fixed copper, through-obstacle reconstruction, exact/reference DRC parity, bounded regional repair, terminal escape, power expansion, and SRJ18/SRJ23 benchmark samples
- Focused Pipeline4 compatibility coverage proving impossible single-layer nodes gain legal board layers without enabling invalid-geometry fallback
- Dependency PR test/type/format checks are green and merge-clean
- Autorouter build, type, format, added-code, Vercel, and Testbox validation checks are green. [All nine Bun test shards pass on the final head](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/32481866749).
