title: Fix already-connected endpoints reserving shared routing regions
description: Fixes autorouting failure by allowing already-connected endpoints to share routing regions instead of reserving them exclusively.
body:
Stacked on #2169.

## Root cause

The tiny-hypergraph adapter inferred that every capacity region containing a connection endpoint belonged exclusively to that endpoint's net.

That is correct for a desired connection endpoint inside its terminal region, but not for an endpoint that is already connected by fanout copper and passed to the next routing stage. The latter only marks where the remaining route begins; owning its large containing region turns shared routing space into a topology barrier across every available layer. Reripping cannot repair a missing graph path.

## Fix

- Desired connection endpoints with `pcb_port_id` keep region ownership.
- Legacy `_containsTarget` desired connection endpoints keep region ownership.
- Regions associated with already-connected copper through `_connectedTo` keep region ownership.
- Endpoints already connected to fanout copper explicitly leave their ordinary containing routing region shared (`netId: -1`), preventing the tiny-hypergraph loader from inferring exclusivity again.

There is no dataset-name check, point-ID prefix check, fallback, solver-order change, or larger iteration budget.

## Real PCB result

Before, the highlighted BA0 net stops at two disconnected fanout stubs:

![Before: disconnected BA0 fanout stubs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/refs/heads/repro/srj29-selective-rerip-exhaustion/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline10-srj29-terminal-region-ownership.snap.svg)

After, the same test runs the normal Pipeline 9 pathing, high-density-routing, and stitching stages, then renders the actual connected solver output with `circuit-to-svg`:

![After: connected BA0 route](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/refs/heads/fix/srj29-terminal-region-ownership-v2/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline10-srj29-terminal-region-ownership.snap.svg)

The highlighted route has zero relaxed-DRC errors.

## Evidence

| Check | Reproduction PR | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Port pathing at 250,000-iteration budget | Exhausted | Solved |
| High-density routing and stitching | Not reached | Completed |
| Highlighted BA0 route relaxed DRC | N/A | 0 errors |

Ten legacy tests that failed under the previous attempted fix now pass with their existing snapshots unchanged, including Pipeline 4, Pipeline 7, SRJ15, SRJ18, SRJ19, SRJ20, bugreport68, bugreport69, bugreport73, bugreport74, and bugreport75 coverage.

The full sample still has eight later pad-to-trace clearance errors from fanout/routing quality. This PR fixes the topological pathing failure only and does not claim that separate issue is solved.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/repro/pipeline10-srj29-terminal-region-ownership.test.ts --timeout 300000`
- Focused legacy tests run one file at a time
- `bunx biome check lib/solvers/PortPointPathingSolver/tinyhypergraph/getRegionNetIdByRegionId.ts tests/repro/pipeline10-srj29-terminal-region-ownership.test.ts`
- `bun run build`

title: Update jscad-electronics to 0.0.155: pin headers mount on the board
description: Fixes the rendering of pin headers by ensuring the plastic body sits on the board with pins standing up, correcting a long-standing visibility issue in the 3D representation.
body:
The pinheader-double-row snapshot has, since it was committed, shown a
16-pin header hanging BENEATH the board: the plastic body was entirely under
the PCB and invisible, with 2mm of pin tip poking up through the holes and
the long pins below. jscad-electronics#333 fixed that — the body sits on the
board with its pins standing up — so this is what the same test now renders.

It was the only 3D image of a pin header anything in the org checked
automatically, which is how the defect survived a year: `<pinheader>` in core
resolves to exactly these `pinrow…` footprint strings, but every other place
they appear in a test suite is 2D. Worth keeping.

0.0.135 to 0.0.155 also brings 32 new part bodies (SOT/SC-70, TO-252/263,
electrolytics, potentiometers, SMD switches, BGA and others), so footprints
that previously rendered as bare pads now render as parts. No other snapshot
in this suite moved: 117 pass.

body:
## Summary

- add `BreadboardClad08mmVias`, a pre-routed breadboard-clad variant with conventional A-E and F-J five-socket terminal strips and breakouts at both ends of every strip
- place 50 independent 0.8 mm vias in four two-via-wide L-shaped corner fields: 12 in each standard corner and 14 in the top-right, whose extra pitch-aligned column fills the long-side space beneath the second mounting hole
- move the four vias in each corner's two innermost long-side columns one 3 mm pitch toward the top or bottom edge, preserving pitch while extending the edge-hugging row
- keep the short arms beside the mounting holes, without connecting any corner via to a breadboard row
- give every via separate 0.15 mm top- and bottom-copper fanouts, using opposite open-area edges on the two layers
- route boundary vias directly and weave recessed fanouts through staggered lanes in the 3 mm via gaps
- route the shifted H2 and both short-arm bottom escapes behind the outer via row before turning inward, preventing those traces from walling off other vias
- terminate every fanout 1 mm beyond the inward edge of its L-shaped via grid, in the open copper/component space between corner fields
- keep every via fanout pointed inward and away from board edges and mounting holes, with no perimeter collection routing
- use 0.8 mm finished holes, 0.9 mm pads, and a 3 mm via pitch, providing 2.1 mm pad-edge spacing and 2.2 mm drill-edge spacing
- export the variant and add its example, checked-in visual snapshot, build/snapshot scripts, documentation, and geometry/connectivity tests

title: Fix selective rerip cycles and prefer caller-owned routes

## Summary

Stacked on #167, the focused bugreport87 reproduction.

- detect repeated selective-rerip owner dependency cycles and escalate to the global rerip path
- retain trace-density region-cost support used by the autorouter's current tiny-hypergraph pin
- add an overridable preservation-preference hook for partial rerips

This combines the solver fix from #168 with the preload-preservation work originally proposed here, so the autorouter dependency has one ready landing PR after #167. It supersedes #168 for landing.

The preservation behavior is a preference, not an immutable-route switch: caller-owned/preloaded routes remain movable when routing cannot otherwise complete.

description: Reduces the time taken for differential-pair collision checks on dense boards from 86 seconds to approximately 28 seconds by optimizing the search algorithm to skip distant obstacles and layer checks.
body:
### Motivation
- Dense boards make the differential-pair search test thousands of possible paths for collisions.

### Before
- Each possible path ran detailed checks against distant obstacles and fixed copper, including copper on other PCB layers. The RV1106G2 reproduction took about 86 seconds.

### After
- The search quickly skips objects that are far away or on another layer, then keeps the same exact collision checks for nearby objects. The routing output stays unchanged and the reproduction completes in about 28 seconds, with a test limit of 45 seconds.

title: Respect existing traces as routed fanout copper
description: Fixes autorouting failure by ensuring that existing routed traces are respected during fanout segment and via selection, preventing collisions with different-net copper.
body:
## Summary

- keep supplied `SimpleRouteJson.traces` as routed copper instead of converting them into obstacles
- check fanout segments and vias directly against existing routed traces during candidate selection and final validation
- preserve same-net behavior using each trace's connection identity and `connectsTo` metadata
- pass existing and newly routed copper to an injected downstream autorouter through `traces`
- require the stacked visual reproduction to escape on the bottom layer with clean independent DRC

No dependency versions change.

## Root cause

Phased `core` routing correctly passes earlier-phase copper in `SimpleRouteJson.traces` while filtering `connections` to the active phase. The fanout solver preserved those traces in its output, but its route search and plan validation did not check them. A later fanout could therefore cross existing different-net copper and still report a valid plan.

Reproduction: #78.

## Fix

`getRoutedTraceCopper` reads wire segments and vias from the supplied traces without changing their SRJ representation. Fanout candidate clearance and final validation compare new plans against that routed copper, including layer spans, trace widths, via diameters, clearance, and same-net identity.

The endpoint-completion handoff now sends `directSrj.traces` to the host-provided autorouter and leaves `obstacles` unchanged. The downstream-router regression asserts that traces are present and that no synthetic `trace-copper:*` obstacles are emitted.

This supersedes the first implementation in this PR, which modeled routed traces as private obstacles. Commit `91140633492efad278e1b4ee451bcde98f6c7227` removes that conversion and implements the reviewed trace-preserving behavior.

## Observable result

| Check | Reproduction #78 | This fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing copper representation | `traces` | remains `traces` |
| Selected escape | top-layer shortcut | via to bottom layer |
| Independent emitted-copper DRC | one different-net collision | clean |
| Downstream router input | n/a | existing/fanout copper in `traces` |

| Before: accepted top-layer collision | After: clean bottom-layer escape |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/repro/fanout-avoids-existing-traces/tests/__snapshots__/existing-trace-clearance-repro.snap.svg) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/fix/fanout-avoids-existing-traces/tests/__snapshots__/existing-trace-clearance-repro.snap.svg) |

Both SVGs render actual solver-emitted PCB copper.

## Verification

- crossing, same-net routed trace, and downstream handoff regressions: 3 passed, 0 failed
- full CI-mode solver suite: 73 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed; 110,916 assertions across 46 files
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- real `@tscircuit/core` phased board reproduction passed with the revised solver source
- focused core fanout/breakout set: 3 passed, 0 failed
- core type-check and build passed

The local non-CI Dataset 07 visual comparison remains a pre-existing mismatch: it reproduces on the exact pre-review commit, while its routing assertions pass. Dataset 07's benchmark-only visual cases are skipped in CI.

## Stack

Depends on #78.

Base: `repro/fanout-avoids-existing-traces` at `1fa5587`.

Head: `fix/fanout-avoids-existing-traces` at `91140633492efad278e1b4ee451bcde98f6c7227`.

## Why this matches phased tscircuit routing

`core` filters `connections` to the active routing phase, then deliberately carries earlier phase copper in `SimpleRouteJson.traces`; its comment says the autorouter owns converting those traces into obstacles. See [`Group.ts` at core 853373fd](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/853373fdcbf4639e8b445eccc9998412774d6f80/lib/components/primitive-components/Group/Group.ts#L1180-L1190).

- `traces` contains the earlier vertical `PRE_ROUTED` copper
- the audit-only SRJ restores `PRE_ROUTED` connection identity without changing any geometry, allowing the independent DRC to distinguish the two nets

This isolates the package boundary rather than reproducing an entire application board.

Existing different-net traces must constrain fanout just like immutable copper obstacles. This fixture provides a safe bottom-layer escape, so the solver should select it instead of accepting the top-layer collision.

title: fix: preserve trace widths when reversing routes
description: Fixes a bug where reversing PCB routes caused incorrect trace widths, ensuring that physical copper widths are preserved during route direction changes.
body:
## Summary

- add one shared, immutable PCB-route reversal helper
- preserve physical copper in both default/constant and interpolated thickness modes when route direction changes
- use it for Group output orientation, trace-by-trace orientation, and both `mergeRoutes` reversal paths
- keep `through_pad` endpoints/layers correct and preserve the unused terminal width of each wire run so reversing twice is lossless

## Root cause and reproduction

In default/constant thickness mode, Circuit JSON stores a wire segment's width on the segment's starting route point. Reversing only the route-point array therefore moves variable widths to the opposite physical segments. In interpolated mode, widths are point-local and must instead remain attached to their points as the route reverses. Core did not distinguish those contracts across four reversal paths:

1. `Group.ensureRouteStartsAtSourceTraceStart`
2. `Trace_doInitialPcbTraceRender.ensureRouteStartsAtObjective`
3. the first-route reversal in `mergeRoutes`
4. the subsequent-route reversal in `mergeRoutes`

The first two had duplicate helpers that handled `through_pad` direction but not thickness-mode semantics; the two `mergeRoutes` paths called `.reverse()` directly and also mutated their input arrays. Group now passes the output trace's `route_thickness_mode` to the shared helper. Trace-by-trace routing and `mergeRoutes` retain the default/constant behavior.

This was reproduced with quick-config's deterministic FR2355 autorouter input (`phase-0.input.simple-route.json`) on current autorouter main. Its 69 output traces contain 28 consecutive wire segments shorter than 0.001 mm, including 2 nm `0.30 -> 0.50 -> 0.30` width transitions. The transition pair comes from `power-trace-expander`; its paired inside/outside points currently keep the pad-neck width safe in either route direction despite Core's raw reversal. It exposed the segment-start-width reversal bug directly.

## Tests

- `reverse-pcb-trace-route.test.ts`: three default/constant variable-width wire runs separated by a via and a through-pad plus an interpolated route; verifies every reversed physical segment/point width, through-pad endpoint/layer reversal, double-reversal identity in both modes, and input immutability
- `merge-routes-variable-width.test.ts`: drives both first-route and subsequent-route reversal branches and verifies widths plus input immutability

Validation completed:

- `bun test tests/utils/reverse-pcb-trace-route.test.ts tests/utils/merge-routes-variable-width.test.ts`
- `bunx biome check` on all six changed files
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`

## Deferred expander cleanup

This PR intentionally does not remove `power-trace-expander`'s `epsilon = Math.min(1e-6, length / 4)` pad-boundary pair. Removing it independently breaks the existing connected-pad safety/coverage regressions because released Core versions can still reverse routes without remapping widths.

After this Core behavior is released and consumed, tscircuit/power-trace-expander#18 can replace the epsilon pair with a normal boundary transition. That follow-up should assert that it introduces no positive wire segment below 1 µm, preserves pad-neck geometry in both route directions, and covers the exact FR2355 input. The unrelated pre-power sub-micron terminal/topology slivers should not be removed by a broad dedupe without separate DRC-backed analysis.

title: Use winding solver by default for implicit breakout points
description: Sets the WindingBreakoutSolver as the default solver for implicit breakout points in the autorouting system, adapting the API and improving the handling of automatic breakouts while reporting infeasibility errors.
body: ## Summary - use `WindingBreakoutSolver` as Core's default implicit breakout-point solver - preserve `autorouter={{ implicitBreakoutPointSolverFn }}` as the highest-priority override - adapt Core's prefixed `regionId` / `connectionId` / `busId` / `targetLayers` contract to the winding package's current API - partition unrelated automatic breakouts into compatible connection cohorts before solving - defer automatic breakout-point rendering until a solve succeeds, preventing phantom points at the origin - report winding infeasibility as an actionable `pcb_autorouting_error` The winding package is currently private and unpublished, so this pins commit `202dbe9e` and bundles it through `tsup.noExternal`. ## Visual audit The counts below are physical vias / rendered PCB trace segments. The third column is the winding-aware hybrid from #3280, included as a concrete alternative for the single-region regressions. | Fixture | `main` legacy | This PR: pure winding default | #3280 hybrid | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | QFP16 + header/passives | 6 / 58 | **0 / 41** | **0 / 37** | clear improvement | | SOT23 regulator | **2 / 40** | 8 / 69 | **2 / 38** | clear regression; this PR also leaves 1 final connection pending | | SOIC8 + I2C header | **2 / 63** | 4 / 66 | 4 / **56** | mild regression / more tangled fanout | ### QFP16: winding is a win The aligned exits remove the old bottom-side via detours. The hybrid alternative gets a slightly smaller route, but both winding approaches are much cleaner than `main`. | `main` | This PR | #3280 hybrid | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | ### SOT23: forcing one edge is a regression All three exits collapse onto the top edge, so VIN/GND/VOUT wrap around the package instead of leaving toward their destinations. The final phase reports `1 CONNECTIONS, 12 TRACES`; the pending connection makes this a blocker before this PR should leave draft. | `main` | This PR | #3280 hybrid | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | ### SOIC8: outside-target order is missing The winding input knows the internal pad positions, but not the external header order. GND/VCC swap as the points are linearized onto the left edge, which introduces a crossing and extra vias. | `main` | This PR | #3280 hybrid | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | The new autorouting-phase SRJ snapshots make the split visible: phase 1 shows pad-to-gate fanout, while phase 2 shows gate-to-destination crossings. ## Weirdness and proposed follow-up PRs 1. **Restore destination-aware behavior for one-region fanouts.** An immediate Core PR can use the #3280 hybrid for single-region breakouts and keep this winding solver for its intended multi-region case. In parallel, a winding-solver PR should accept an outside continuation target per connection and assign edges per connection/bus (keeping buses and differential pairs atomic). That should retain the QFP improvement without the SOT23 edge collapse. 2. **Propagate the selected layer end to end.** Winding returns `layer`, but `pcb_breakout_point` has no layer and SRJ currently hard-codes automatic breakout points to `top`. A circuit-json + Core PR should add the field, store it here, consume it for both SRJ endpoint branches, and keep it synchronized when fanout moves an exit. 3. **Make exact gate placement obstacle-aware.** The old solver considered pads and used boundary intervals; winding currently receives only region bounds/endpoints. A winding/Core PR can use winding for topology/order/layer, followed by an obstacle-aware boundary-slot placer. 4. **Publish and align the winding package contract.** Rename its input IDs to the prefixed props names, replace `preferredLayers` with `targetLayers`, publish a release, and then remove this adapter and Git-SHA dependency. 5. **Make the callback contract synchronous.** `@tscircuit/props` currently permits a Promise even though Core layout rejects async solver output. ## Validation - `bun test tests/breakout --timeout 120000` — 19 pass, 2 skip - `bunx tsc --noEmit` - `bun run build` - `bun test --timeout 120000` — 1,429 pass, 40 skip, 0 fail Related: #3304, #3280, #3350

title: fix: keep routed vias out of SRJ obstacles
description: Fixes the issue of routed child-subcircuit vias being incorrectly emitted as obstacles in SRJ, ensuring they are preserved in traces instead.
body:
## Summary

- keep routed child-subcircuit vias in SRJ `traces` without also emitting the same copper in `obstacles`
- suppress a via obstacle only when its PCB trace ID, circuit-world coordinate, and complete layer span match a preserved trace via
- preserve custom via pad/hole diameters from either Circuit JSON or SRJ field names
- verify Pipeline7 and Pipeline9 phase inputs keep an identical obstacle set while accumulated traces contain vias

## Root cause

[tscircuit-autorouter#2192](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2192) captured a full Game Boy parent-routing SRJ from `@tscircuit/core@0.0.1730` with 379 obstacles and 136 preloaded traces.

The input contains 88 `pcb_via` obstacles and 88 `route_type: "via"` points in the preloaded traces. Their coordinate multisets match exactly, so every routed via is represented twice. Core was preserving each routed child `pcb_trace` in `traces` while independently converting every corresponding `pcb_via` record into an obstacle.

Same-group phased routing is already correct after #3021: a fixed base SRJ is reused and prior phase output is appended only to `traces`. The new parity assertions lock in that behavior and prove the inputs actually contain routed vias.

Pipeline9 already handles preloaded trace vias directly when building its topology and deliberately avoids the Pipeline7 trace-to-obstacle preprocessing path, so no autorouter change is needed.

## Safety

Explicit/assignable vias and unmatched geometry remain obstacles. Matching includes the full normalized layer span, so a stacked via at the same coordinate on another span is preserved. Custom via dimensions remain on the SRJ trace after the duplicate obstacle is removed.

## Validation

- focused SRJ/via tests: 5 passed
- Game Boy-like and child-subcircuit routing integrations: 2 passed
- fanout and Arduino imported-region reroute snapshots regenerated and visually verified: 2 passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- targeted `bunx biome check`
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`

With `TEST_PIPELINE7_PIPELINE9_PARITY=1`, Pipeline7 passed all assertions with 13 phase inputs holding the same 116 obstacles. Pipeline9 completed all 18 phases with the same 116 obstacles; preloaded trace vias reached 70 and the final topology reduced them to 66. Its structural assertions passed before the existing visual snapshot comparison reported 3.27% drift against a 2% threshold, so this PR does not rewrite that unrelated snapshot.

title: Fix concurrent builds in Bun workers
description: Fixes build failures in concurrent Bun workers by removing the dependency on process.chdir(projectDir) and passing project directory explicitly to path-sensitive helpers.
body:
## What changed

Remove the worker-thread dependency on `process.chdir(projectDir)` from concurrent build and snapshot execution. Thread the project directory explicitly through path-sensitive helpers instead.

The affected helpers now resolve paths relative to the supplied project directory for:

- userland `react`/`tscircuit` module resolution;
- static asset loading and `tsconfig.json` `baseUrl`;
- KiCad footprint/model URL conversion;
- circuit JSON generation and snapshot generation.

Sequential callers retain the same behavior through the default `process.cwd()` fallback.

## Root cause

The concurrent worker handlers called `process.chdir(projectDir)`. This worked with Bun `1.3.14`, but Bun `1.4.0` rejects `process.chdir()` inside worker threads with:

```text
process.chdir() is not supported in workers
```

The failure was exposed by `tscircuit/sparkfun-boards` after its CI environment picked up Bun `1.4.0`. The CLI worker code had contained this call since the concurrent build worker implementation, so pinning Bun would only mask the compatibility issue.

## Why this approach

Workers should not mutate process-global working-directory state. Passing absolute project paths makes worker behavior deterministic, supports multiple projects safely, and remains compatible with Bun versions that prohibit `process.chdir()` in workers.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit --pretty false`
- `git diff --check`
- `bun test ./tests/cli/build/build-with-concurrency-client-server-pattern.test.ts`
  - 1 test passed
  - 3 concurrent workers completed circuit JSON, GLB, and preview generation
  - build exited successfully

This addresses the build failure observed in [tscircuit/sparkfun-boards#324](https://github.com/tscircuit/sparkfun-boards/pull/324).

## Summary

- record segment-level mutation provenance for accepted Pipeline9 regional and hypergraph changes, carrying it through later fixed-route splices
- add a second, stock `TraceSimplificationSolver` stage after new-trace simplification that edits only maximal contiguous mutated preload regions
- keep untouched preload copper, jumpers, through-obstacle routes, point separators, and already-simplified new traces immutable collision context
- preserve splice endpoints and handle collapsed same-boundary hairpins without broadening the editable region
- make spatial-index broad-phase queries account for indexed copper radius so local simplification cannot miss a neighboring-bucket blocker

## Why

Pipeline9 can mutate a preloaded trace during regional fallback, but the existing simplification stage treats all updated preloads as immutable `otherHdRoutes`. In the dense RP2040 parity fixture that allowed a short top-bottom-top excursion on `source_trace_10_0` to bypass the normal useless-via pass.

This supersedes #2194. Instead of cleaning an entire mutated trace with a custom pass, this PR persists exact mutation masks, forms local editable windows, and runs the regular simplification pipeline on those windows only.

## Verification

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- all Pipeline9 feature tests: 48/48 passed, 540 assertions
- bugreport96 full Game Boy fixture: passed 10 assertions; routed snapshot updated
- dense core parity fixture: all 18 phases completed, obstacle count stayed constant, 60 final vias, 0 autorouting errors; the highlighted vias at `(8.443, -4.145)` and `(8.847, -4.447)` are absent and `source_trace_10_0` ends with 2 vias
- the linked core visual snapshot changes by 2.80%, as expected from the simplified routing output; that core snapshot should be updated after consuming the released autorouter

It still has 32 relaxed-DRC findings, so this PR fixes completion rather than claiming DRC-clean routing. !Full Game Boy routed with Pipeline 9(https:raw.githubusercontent.comAbse2001tscircuit-autoroutercodexfix-full-gameboy-pipeline9testsbugs__snapshots__bugreport96-full-gameboy-no-breakout-routed.snap.svg)  Validation bun test --timeout 9999999 testsbugsbugreport96-full-gameboy-no-breakout.test.ts bun test --timeout 9999999 testsfeaturespipeline9-high-density-regional-fallback.test.ts testsfeaturespipeline9-high-density-no-invalid-fallback.test.ts testsfeaturespipeline9-regional-fallback-target-layers.test.ts testsfeaturespipeline9-regular-regional-fallback-fixed-preload.test.ts bunx tsc --noEmit bun run build bun run format:check git diff --check
body:
## Summary

- preserve an original fixed section when a grid-based regional solver merges it with electrically equivalent same-net copper and emits no separately named replacement
- include every preserved section in candidate copper-conflict validation before accepting the regional result
- count only sections that were actually replaced in rerouting statistics
- regenerate the full no-breakout Game Boy input from `tscircuit@0.0.2384` (`@tscircuit/core@0.0.1730`, autorouter `0.0.830`)
- convert the refreshed full no-breakout Game Boy regression to a passing routed snapshot

Depends on #2192. Until that repro-only PR merges, this stacked PR also displays its fixture commits. After #2192 merges, this PR will reduce to the fix commits.

## Root cause

The full Game Boy repro reaches a small regional node containing two almost coincident fixed sections on the same root net. HighDensity A01/A03 rasterize both sections into the same grid cells and intentionally emit one physical route. Pipeline 9 previously required exactly one named replacement for every movable fixed section and failed with `expected one replacement ... got 0` even though the omitted original copper could remain safely in place.

The change does not discard or invent copper. A section with no replacement remains unchanged and is added back to the fixed-route collision set. A candidate that conflicts with it still fails or retries through the existing explicit promotion path. Multiple replacements remain an invariant violation.

## Result

The refreshed 21-connection, 379-obstacle, 136-preloaded-trace Game Boy parent board now routes without breakout points in about 179 seconds. The routed output contains 140 traces and 153 vias. It still has 32 relaxed-DRC findings, so this PR fixes completion rather than claiming DRC-clean routing.

![Full Game Boy routed with Pipeline 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Abse2001/tscircuit-autorouter/codex/fix-full-gameboy-pipeline9/tests/bugs/__snapshots__/bugreport96-full-gameboy-no-breakout-routed.snap.svg)

## Validation

- `bun test --timeout 9999999 tests/bugs/bugreport96-full-gameboy-no-breakout.test.ts`
- `bun test --timeout 9999999 tests/features/pipeline9-high-density-regional-fallback.test.ts tests/features/pipeline9-high-density-no-invalid-fallback.test.ts tests/features/pipeline9-regional-fallback-target-layers.test.ts tests/features/pipeline9-regular-regional-fallback-fixed-preload.test.ts`

No fallback or board-specific behavior enableBroadFallback: false prevents broad input generation, validation, and execution. No circuit IDs, fixed coordinates, restart strategies, or board-specific conditions. Every speculative local candidate is accepted only after complete DRC evaluation.  Exact regressions  Board  Initial  Baseline  Final  Broad attemptedaccepted   ---  ---:  ---:  ---:  ---   circuit143  2  1  0  false  false   circuit144  1  0  0  false  false  The generic three-layer regression places the error center on a nearer inner-layer segment while the real conflict is on bottom copper. Both targeted-force and safe-layer paths must choose the layer-compatible segment and reach DRC 0.  Current-main compatibility Based on repair03 main 19c61d3 Preserves bugreport93 repair e12df3b6 Upstream targeted different-net-via tests pass alongside both dataset regressions  Validation bun test  68 passed, 0 failed, 509 assertions bun run typecheck bun run formatcheck Full Pipeline7 circuit143  external relaxed DRC 0 Full Pipeline7 circuit144  exact 1  0 in one targeted candidate; external relaxed DRC 0 Broad input absent; broad attemptedaccepted: false  false
body:
## Impact

Clears Pipeline7's exact-repair clearance failures without broad routing:

- dataset01 circuit143: chained trace/via conflict;
- dataset01 circuit144: bottom-pad conflict beside a nearer wrong-layer trace segment.

This keeps `enableBroadFallback: false` honest while preventing the dataset result from trading the circuit143 fix for a new circuit144 failure.

## Root causes and fixes

### Chained trace/via conflict

Circuit143 enters exact repair with two DRC errors. The targeted pass improves that to one, but moving the trace exposes a nearby movable-via conflict. Either edit alone fails; the valid candidate needs both edits.

The bounded displacement chain detours the conflicting trace, moves only the newly blocking movable via, derives its motion from measured clearance geometry, and accepts the composite candidate only after full-board DRC scoring.

### Wrong-layer pad selection

Circuit144's pad error center is geometrically closer to an inner/top-side segment than to the actual bottom-layer segment touching the same transition. Repair previously selected the nearest segment first, then rejected the bottom pad because its layer did not match that incorrectly selected segment.

Repair now resolves a foreign obstacle/trace pair together and selects the nearest reported-route segment only from layers where the obstacle exists. Direct `pcb_pad_trace_clearance_error` inputs are recognized structurally, and obstacle layers use the full board layer mapping rather than assuming `z=1` is always bottom.

## No fallback or board-specific behavior

- `enableBroadFallback: false` prevents broad input generation, validation, and execution.
- No circuit IDs, fixed coordinates, restart strategies, or board-specific conditions.
- Every speculative local candidate is accepted only after complete DRC evaluation.

## Exact regressions

| Board | Initial | Baseline | Final | Broad attempted/accepted |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| circuit143 | 2 | 1 | 0 | false / false |
| circuit144 | 1 | 0 | 0 | false / false |

The generic three-layer regression places the error center on a nearer inner-layer segment while the real conflict is on bottom copper. Both targeted-force and safe-layer paths must choose the layer-compatible segment and reach DRC 0.

## Current-main compatibility

- Based on repair03 `main` `19c61d3`
- Preserves bugreport93 repair `e12df3b6`
- Upstream targeted different-net-via tests pass alongside both dataset regressions

## Validation

- `bun test` — **68 passed, 0 failed, 509 assertions**
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run formatcheck`
- Full Pipeline7 circuit143 — external relaxed DRC **0**
- Full Pipeline7 circuit144 — exact **1 → 0** in one targeted candidate; external relaxed DRC **0**
- Broad input absent; broad attempted/accepted: **false / false**

title: Fix strict indexed access in Dinic level checks
description: Fixes TypeScript type-checking errors related to indexed access in the Dinic algorithms level checks by adding non-null assertions to ensure valid indices are used.
body:
## Summary

Add non-null assertions to the two `levels` array reads in `Dinic.buildLevels`.

## Why this is needed

Downstream consumers such as `tscircuit/sparkfun-boards` compile this package source through its TypeScript export. With `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`, TypeScript models indexed array access as `T | undefined`, even when the surrounding algorithm guarantees that the index is valid. This produced:

```text
lib/route-single-layer-adaptive-exits.ts(285,35): error TS2532: Object is possibly undefined
lib/route-single-layer-adaptive-exits.ts(290,12): error TS2532: Object is possibly undefined
```

The first access checks `this.levels[edge.to]` while traversing an edge from `this.edges[node]`. `edge.to` is a graph node created and managed within the solver, so it is a valid index into the levels array. The second access checks `this.levels[sink]`, where `sink` is the method parameter representing the destination node and is likewise a valid graph-node index.

The existing code already uses non-null assertions for the corresponding queue, edge, and level accesses in this method. These two assertions make the same invariant explicit to TypeScript; they do not alter runtime behavior and do not disable strict checking globally.

## Validation

- `git diff --check` passes.
- The two downstream TS2532 diagnostics are eliminated by the change.
- The repository-wide type check currently reports unrelated baseline dependency/environment errors involving `bun:test`, Bun globals, and `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter` API mismatches.

This fixes the type-check failure reported by [tscircuit/sparkfun-boards#324](https://github.com/tscircuit/sparkfun-boards/pull/324).

The MBOM carries a resolved part number but groups on the designation, because unlike the EBOM it groups and so its row count must not depend on a lookup. body:
Adds `<enclosure.screwboss>` to a PCB mounting hole and proposes a
manufacturing BOM for the enclosure, separate from the board's EBOM.

Authoring
- A screw boss is declared in the hole that needs it. The render derives the
  boss geometry plus the screw, insert and spacer it consumes; there are no
  hardware elements to author, because a fastener's length and insert series
  are not knowable before the enclosure resolves.
- Two dotted namespaces: `enclosure.*` for what an enclosure makes or consumes,
  `assembly.*` for what a device does. An element goes in the namespace of the
  thing that consumes it.
- `<assembly.component>` covers every device part. A relationship is a child
  element and a property is a prop, so only a new prop surface earns a new
  element.

Records
- One `source_component` per physical piece; a piece that renders also gets one
  `cad_component`, which holds the model string. Three new ftypes
  (`assembly_device`, `assembly_enclosure`, `assembly_part`), two new fields on
  `source_component_base` (`parent_source_component_id`, `designation`), one on
  `cad_component` (`modelprinter_string`).
- `pcb_component_id` is the frame a piece renders in; `source_component_id` is
  the piece. Pieces borrow the frame of their nearest framed ancestor, so the
  enclosure keeps the `pcb_component` it emits today and parts with no position
  get no `cad_component` and do not render.

Identity
- A BOM line is identified by `manufacturer_part_number` if set, otherwise
  `designation`. This is the same specification-resolved-to-catalogue-part
  pipeline the EBOM already runs through `partsEngine`, which gains a
  `modelprinterString` parameter.
- The MBOM carries a resolved part number but groups on the designation,
  because unlike the EBOM it groups and so its row count must not depend on a
  lookup.

Export
- `convertCircuitJsonToMbomRows` / `convertMbomRowsToCsv` alongside the existing
  EBOM pair. The EBOM is unchanged except that it, and the pick-and-place file,
  now exclude assembly-class parts — today an enclosure appears in both.

Implementation detail, measurements and staging are in a companion document
that is not part of this PR.

description: Adds an optional schPinLabelFontSize prop to port for specifying the font size of schematic pin labels, allowing for better control over label visibility without affecting other components.
body:
## What this adds

Adds an optional `schPinLabelFontSize` prop to `<port>`.

Each `<port>` represents one schematic pin, so a numeric prop here is already per-pin. This is narrower and less ambiguous than a `Record<PinLabel, number>`, especially when imported symbols contain repeated aliases.

The value is:

- optional and remains `undefined` when omitted
- expressed in schematic millimeters, matching the existing renderer font-size units
- validated as a positive, finite number with Zod

## Note

This PR only introduces the prop definition. Core and circuit-to-svg do not consume it yet I’ll handle those integrations in separate follow-up PRs if this pr is valid

## Why

Imported EasyEDA symbols can have long pin labels that do not fit in the available stem space. Scaling the whole symbol or changing the global renderer font size can affect unrelated symbols.

This prop provides an explicit per-port override without changing existing components. Follow-up changes can carry it through circuit-json/core, let circuit-to-svg read it when present, and let easyeda-converter compute a suitable value from the imported label width and available space. No part-specific value or collision heuristic is added here.

Related converter work: https://github.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/pull/482

description: Add board-level option to allow the autorouter to generate blind and buried vias, defaulting to false to restrict newly generated vias to the full board stack.
body:
## Summary

- add the board-level `allowBlindAndBuriedVias` boolean
- default it to `false`, so ordinary boards request full-stack generated vias unless they explicitly opt in
- clarify that `CopperPourProps.unbroken` reserves a pour during autorouting while allowing vias to cross through antipads
- regenerate the public component and props references

## Contract

`allowBlindAndBuriedVias={false}` is the default and restricts newly generated vias to the full board stack. Setting it to `true` allows the autorouter to generate blind and buried vias when the fabrication process supports them.

To keep an unrelated trace from splitting a copper pour, board authors can mark the pour `unbroken`; vias may still cross the reserved region using antipads.

## Cross-repository stack

- Circuit JSON field: [tscircuit/circuit-json#719](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/719)

The regression test uses EasyEDA component C2848306 (`SHT40-AD1B-R3`), where EP pin 5 is marked with `visibility: "none"`.

- EP pin 5 is absent from the generated schematic

title: repro: hidden EasyEDA pins render as visible schematic pins
description: Fixes the rendering issue where EasyEDA hidden pins are incorrectly displayed as visible schematic pins in the generated TSX.
body:
## Summary

Adds a focused visual reproduction for C2848306 (`SHT40-AD1B-R3`).

EasyEDA marks the exposed-pad schematic pin as hidden:

```text
P~none~0~5~...~EP~...
```

The parser retains `visibility: "none"`, but generated TSX still contains:

```tsx
pin5: ["EP"]
```

As a result, tscircuit renders EP as an ordinary visible schematic pin.

## Expected behavior

The PCB die-pad geometry may remain in the footprint, but a pin marked `none` by EasyEDA should not become a normal visible schematic terminal.

EasyEDA documents the second pin configuration field as whether the pin is displayed, and its symbol documentation says disabling **Show** hides the pin when placed on the schematic canvas:

body:
## Stack

Stacked on #2177. Depends on [tscircuit/power-trace-expander#19](https://github.com/tscircuit/power-trace-expander/pull/19) at immutable commit `1dbee80833324a6056f19746f8a910512eb02a76`.

Merge order:

1. merge the reproduction PR #2177;
2. merge power-trace-expander #19;
3. update this dependency pin if #19 lands under a different merge SHA, then merge this PR.

## Changes

- update only `@tscircuit/power-trace-expander` from baseline commit `6fa2ac79cf13129c47432db3a23e61c17067e912` to the budget-aware fix commit;
- activate the focused `bugreport98` regression captured from the MangoPi R3C six-layer route;
- assert that power expansion completes inside the unchanged 8,000,000-iteration budget and preserves all 405 trace records.

The diff against #2177 is intentionally limited to `package.json` and the focused bugreport98 test.

## Result

The exact focused stage input that previously failed with `PowerTraceExpanderSolver ran out of iterations` now:

- solves without an error;
- stops optional expansion at its reserved budget;
- completes cleanup and direction-independent clearance repair;
- does not use the emergency final-acceptance fallback;
- reports `completionReason: "expansion_budget"` and `resultStatus: "best_effort"`;
- returns 405 traces with 405 unique trace IDs.

The total solver limit remains 8,000,000 iterations. This change does not increase it.

## Validation

```text
bun test tests/bugs/bugreport98-mangopi-r3c-power-expansion-iteration-limit.test.ts --timeout 9999999
# 1 pass, 0 fail; 87.4s

bunx tsc --noEmit
# pass

bun run build
# pass
```

## Scope

This verifies the isolated power-expansion stage only. `best_effort` is not a DRC or fabrication guarantee. The complete MangoPi board has not produced an accepted routed Circuit JSON or validated manufacturing outputs, so it remains **DO NOT FABRICATE**.

## Focused stage repro (`bugreport98`)

This fixture is the exact two-element constructor tuple captured at pipeline definition index 21:

1. the six-layer pre-power SRJ, including 405 pre-power trace records and an empty `fixedTraces` array;
2. the exact `PowerTraceExpanderOptions` with `allowNewVias: false` and 20 selected power connections.

| Property | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Layers | 6 |
| Connections | 113 |
| Terminals | 518 |
| Pre-power trace records | 405 |
| Fixed traces | 0 |
| Selected power connections | 20 |
| Constructor tuple SHA-256 | `6e6ee35e29f1a7b0ddf1586ff7a04646fd7476ebfe0627f37c666ccfb59e85a7` |

The fixture instantiates the repository-internal `PowerTraceExpansionSolver` directly, avoiding the preceding multi-minute pipeline stages.

## Expected behavior

Power expansion is a successive approximation. Approaching its iteration limit should preserve budget for required finalization and return the best committed result with explicit quality/status metadata. Simply increasing the iteration limit is not the intended fix.

## Validation

```text
bun test tests/bugs/bugreport97-mangopi-r3c-six-layer-power-expansion.test.ts tests/bugs/bugreport98-mangopi-r3c-power-expansion-iteration-limit.test.ts
# 0 fail; 2 intentionally skipped

bunx tsc --noEmit
# pass

bun run build
# pass
```

## Scope

The earlier high-density fixture is not a confirmed nontermination bug; it solved in the debugger after 765.422 seconds and 5,878,583 iterations. The reproducible failure is the final power-expansion iteration policy and memory-heavy failed-candidate retention.

This PR does not produce an accepted routed board or manufacturing output. The MangoPi board remains **DO NOT FABRICATE**.

title: Repair Pipeline7 chained trace/via and layer-specific pad clearance conflicts
description: Fixes autorouting failure by enabling Pipeline7 to handle trace and via conflicts more effectively, ensuring DRC compliance without fallback.
body:
## Summary

Pipeline7 now uses repair03's exact, DRC-scored repairs for two related clearance cases:

- move a conflicting trace and its newly blocking movable via as one candidate;
- select the route segment on a layer shared with the offending pad or obstacle.

Pipeline7 uses one bounded exact-repair portfolio with broad fallback explicitly disabled. The shared adaptive wrapper remains available for Pipeline9, but Pipeline7 no longer routes through it. There are no circuit IDs, fixed coordinates, DRC filters, or board-specific production branches.

## Why

For circuit143, moving the trace alone exposed a nearby via conflict, while moving the via alone did not clear the original conflict. Repair03 now scores the combined trace/via move before accepting it.

For circuit144, the DRC error center could be closer to a segment on the wrong layer than to the segment involved in the pad conflict. Repair03 now resolves the obstacle and compatible route layer together. Current autorouter `main` clears this board before exact repair, and the integration regression verifies it stays clean without broad fallback.

## Results

Same-machine dataset01 benchmark ([run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/32457260621)):

| Metric | Main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Relaxed DRC pass | 84/85 (98.8%) | 85/85 (100%) |
| DRC issues | 1 | 0 |
| circuit143 / sample58 | 1 DRC | 0 DRC |

After merging the latest autorouter `main` and pinning the upstream repair03 merge commit, a fresh local Pipeline7 dataset01 run remains **85/85 DRC-clean with 0 timeouts**.

## Validation

- Pipeline7 focused integration tests: 3 passed, 0 failed.
- Pipeline9 compatibility tests: 3 passed, 0 failed, including the bounded SRJ18 precision regression.
- Local Pipeline7 dataset01 benchmark: 85/85 completed, 85/85 relaxed-DRC passed, 0 timeouts.
- repair03: 81 passed, 0 failed; typecheck and format check pass.
- Autorouter CI is running on the final pushed commit.

## Dependency

title: Finalize the best power-trace result within the iteration budget
description: Reserves the final eighth of the existing 8,000,000-step budget for cleanup and direction-independent clearance repair, returning the last committed approximation instead of failing when optional width expansion reaches its share of the budget.
body:
## Summary

- reserve the final eighth of the existing 8,000,000-step budget for cleanup and direction-independent clearance repair
- return the last committed approximation instead of failing when optional width expansion reaches its share of the budget
- make cleanup and clearance repair successive too, preserving their committed prefixes if their sub-budgets are reached
- cap retained failed-child solver objects at 16 while reporting the full cumulative failure count
- expose explicit expansion/finalization statuses and `complete` versus `best_effort` result quality

This does **not** increase the iteration limit.

## Root cause

The MangoPi R3C six-layer route reaches `PowerTraceExpanderSolver` with 405 pre-power traces and 245 selected traces. The solver spent all 8,000,000 iterations in optional expansion, then inherited `BaseSolver`'s empty final-acceptance hook and converted a valid committed approximation into `ran out of iterations`.

The same run retained every rejected grid solver. The baseline kept about 47,000 child solvers and their grids alive, growing the heap to roughly 8 GB before failure.

## Exact MangoPi regression

The whole-board and focused constructor fixtures are captured in [tscircuit-autorouter#2177](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2177). The dependency update and active passing regression are isolated in the stacked [tscircuit-autorouter#2207](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2207).

Baseline:

- failed at exactly 8,000,000 iterations
- first expansion pass was still in progress
- about 47,000 failed child solvers retained
- multi-gigabyte heap growth / OOM risk

This fix, using the unchanged 8,000,000 total cap:

- solved the power-expansion stage in 7,343,448 iterations
- stopped optional expansion at 7,000,000 iterations
- completed cleanup and clearance repair normally
- left 656,552 iterations unused
- reported 42,978 cumulative failed candidates while retaining only 16 solver objects
- finished at about 495 MB heap used / 1.16 GB RSS in the measured run
- returned a deterministic 405-trace result

The result intentionally reports `resultStatus: "best_effort"`, 213 unresolved via cleanups, and 32 unresolved conservative trace-clearance segments. Downstream routing DRC remains authoritative; this change prevents an optimizer-budget failure but does not claim fabrication validity.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- all new and affected budget/finalization tests pass
- exact 4.2 MB MangoPi stage replay passes twice with byte-identical output
- repository functional assertions pass; the existing RP2040 wall-clock guard measured 20.26 s on this branch versus 20.99 s on unmodified main on this host, so the host itself is currently above that test's 20 s threshold

## Related PRs

- [tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2177](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2177) — reproduction-only whole-board and focused MangoPi fixtures
- [tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2207](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2207) — stacked dependency update and active focused regression

title: Fix bottom ground-pour shorts
description: Fixes ground-pour shorts caused by incorrect attribution of routed traces to the ground plane, ensuring proper routing of GND connections and avoiding signal trace conflicts.
body:
## Summary

- upgrade `tscircuit` from `0.0.2212` to `0.0.2387` (`@tscircuit/core` `0.0.1588` to `0.0.1734`), which includes the layer-aware route attribution fix from [tscircuit/core#3024](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3024)
- route top-side GND connections into the bottom ground plane in a dedicated fanout phase instead of building a board-spanning GND minimum-spanning tree
- preserve the bottom-mounted coin-cell ground pad as already connected to the bottom pour
- rotate the LF crystal to avoid crossed oscillator routes and move the antenna 0.25 mm inward for the current board-edge DRC

## Root cause

The old core attributed routed traces by checking whether their endpoints overlapped a pad without filtering pads by copper layer. The 10 x 10 mm bottom GND pad on the coin-cell holder therefore claimed top-layer signal routes whose endpoints happened to lie above it. The ground-pour solver then treated those signal traces and their vias as GND, producing the apparent plane-wide short.

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck`
- clean-cache `bun run build`
- `bun run build -- --all-images`
- zero `*error` elements in the generated circuit JSON
- Gerber-mode short checks pass on both top and bottom layers
- exported Gerbers contain no non-GND via connections or bottom signal-trace intersections with the GND pour

The build still reports the pre-existing advisory warnings for unnamed traces, footprint metadata, and three autorouted length limits; none are shorts or DRC errors.

Circuit JSON already marks intentionally unconnected pins with `source_port.do_not_connect`. The Altium converter was ignoring that field, so generated schematics did not show the red X at those pins.

## Why it is done this way

The converter finds each `schematic_port` linked to a source port where `do_not_connect` is true and writes Altium's native red thin-cross record at that schematic port's position.

This reuses the existing Circuit JSON meaning instead of adding another schema element. It also ties the cross to a real port instead of guessing from a free coordinate.

- render `source_port.do_not_connect` as native Altium red crosses
- test the native record fields and exact pin-terminal position

- SimpleFOC Shield V3: 0

The remaining HERON source crosses are on electrical points that the test importer does not yet model as source and schematic ports. This PR does not force them through a new Circuit JSON type.

title: Use active breakout bounds for copper pours
description: Changes the copper pour obstacle selection process to use the active routing PCB group ID, ensuring that only relevant copper pours are included while preserving existing non-pour obstacles and routing behavior.
body:
## Summary

- use the active `routingPcbGroupId` only to select and clip outline-less unbroken copper-pour obstacles for each breakout phase
- preserve the existing full subcircuit-wide non-pour obstacle list exactly
- preserve previously accumulated sibling breakout traces and the existing global-phase behavior
- leave connections, buses, targets, layers, bounds, routing rules, and phase filtering unchanged

## Implementation

The base SRJ remains unchanged. For a phase with `routingPcbGroupId`, Core regenerates only the unbroken copper-pour obstacles using that PCB group, removes only the old `isCopperPour` entries from the phase input, and appends the corrected pours. The group ID is not used for component, pad, via, keepout, cutout, trace, connection, or bus filtering.

The fix uses explicit `if` control flow for active-group selection and phase-local pour replacement.

## AM62L validation

Validated against the latest merged `simplified-am62l-computer` `index.circuit.tsx` with this branch linked locally:

- SoC: 988 obstacles = 986 unchanged non-pours + 2 GND pours at center `(2, 1)`, size `21.300000000000004 x 21.300000000000004 mm`
- RAM: 988 obstacles = 986 unchanged non-pours + 2 GND pours at center `(29.675, 0.949083)`, size `24.05 x 19.200000000000003 mm`
- both inputs: 33 connections, 3 ordered buses, 8 layers, and 0 traces in the diagnostic zero-output capture
- canonical non-pour SHA-256 for old/new SoC and RAM: `c2a4fbf54853706cfa1d72f14a435f56e309aabb9fa5b3821929b3ba8b15a9b2`
- the entire SoC SRJ is canonically identical to the prior 988-obstacle fixture
- RAM non-obstacle content and all 986 non-pour obstacles are canonically identical to the prior fixture; only its two pour objects move from the SoC bounds to the RAM bounds

The existing SoC fanout solver failure at `route_top_layer_dogbones` 23/33 is independent of this correction.

The schematic trace solver correctly moved the U1-side GP17 label and emitted its short connector after the dependency bump. Core then lost the source-trace identity of port-only solver labels: the collapsed global net could select the outer LCD_CS connectivity key for the internal GP17 label, and fallback reconciliation could consume a label belonging to the other endpoint. Core now retains the exact source trace and its connectivity key for unambiguous port-only placements. Ambiguous multi-trace ports deliberately receive no inferred owner.

title: fix: preserve implicit breakout layers in autorouting
description: Fixes loss of selected routing layer in autorouting for implicit breakout points, ensuring correct layer is used in Circuit JSON emission.
body:
## Dependency

Depends on tscircuit/circuit-json#722 and its npm release: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/722

Until that release is available and Core updates its registry dependency, typecheck/CI may fail because the published `PcbBreakoutPoint` type does not yet include `layer`.

## Summary

- carry the layer selected by the implicit breakout-point solver into native `pcb_breakout_point.layer`
- use that Circuit JSON layer in both child breakout routing and parent cross-boundary SRJ endpoints
- preserve the existing pad-layer or `top` fallback for legacy/manual breakout points with no layer

## Problem

Core passes bus `preferredLayers` into the implicit solver, which returns each placement with `solvedPoint.layer`. Previously the layer was lost before Circuit JSON emission, so later SimpleRouteJson conversion could emit the breakout target on `top` even when the solver selected an inner layer.

The selected routing layer now lives with the breakout point’s x/y routing constraint in Circuit JSON. This avoids mutable sidecar state and avoids scanning the live component tree during SRJ conversion.

## Checks

Run locally against the linked circuit-json producer branch:

- `bun test tests/breakout` (19 pass, 2 skipped)
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- targeted `bunx biome check` on the four changed production files
- `bun run build`
- focused AM62L byte-1 route: 11 SoC fanouts, 11 RAM fanouts, and 11 global routes with zero autorouter errors
- layer consistency: 11/11 matched; shorts check: none

## Summary

- update `circuit-json-to-footprinter` to `0.0.54`
- update `@tscircuit/footprinter` to `0.0.426`
- update the circular-pad regression fixture to provide the radius required by current Circuit JSON
- remove the CLI-specific code that copied `@tscircuit/manifold-2d/manifold.wasm` into `dist/cli`

## Related upstream fixes

- [tscircuit/manifold-2d#12](https://github.com/tscircuit/manifold-2d/pull/12) makes Manifold use its embedded WASM bytes in bundled Node environments.
- [tscircuit/circuit-json-to-footprinter#109](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-footprinter/pull/109) updates the intermediate package to consume the fixed `@tscircuit/manifold-2d@0.0.8` release.

`circuit-json-to-footprinter` brings `@tscircuit/manifold-2d` into the CLI bundle. The previous Manifold Node loader searched for a separate `manifold.wasm` beside the generated CLI entrypoint, but Bun bundles JavaScript without automatically copying that transitive runtime asset. The CLI briefly worked around this by resolving and copying Manifold's internal WASM file during its build.

WASM initialization belongs to `@tscircuit/manifold-2d`, not the CLI. With the two upstream fixes released, the packed CLI is self-contained and no longer needs dependency-specific asset-copying logic.

## Validation

title: Fix RP2040 crystal zero-via routing
description: Fixes routing of RP2040 crystal connections to ensure zero vias are used, preventing routing errors in PCB design.
body:

- route RP2040 crystal X1/X2 connections in the first routing phase
- use semantic crystal pin aliases instead of physical pin numbers
- refresh all PCB, schematic, and 3D snapshots

## Why
The RP2040 crystal signal traces require zero vias. When those traces were routed together with the rest of the module, the default router could produce two-via routes and then report that the maximum via count was exceeded. Assigning the X1/X2 connection group to phase 0 lets the default autorouter reserve legal direct crystal paths before routing the remaining nets.

title: fix: skip unmeasurable cross-layer meander candidates
description: Fixes a regression that caused the solver to throw an error when encountering unmeasurable cross-layer meander candidates by returning a null sentinel instead.
body:
## Summary

- return a `null` sentinel when a meander candidate has no paired planar geometry on its layer
- classify that candidate as `no-paired-same-layer-geometry` with no ranking score, then continue the normal candidate search
- preserve the existing zero-length and invalid-cost invariant errors

## Root cause

The regression merged in #52 creates tunable segments on two layers, while the paired route has planar copper on only one of them. The first cross-layer candidate reached centerline scoring before a later same-layer candidate and threw because there was no paired geometry to measure on that layer.

Missing same-layer geometry is candidate-specific, so this change rejects only that candidate. It does not assign a fabricated zero distance cost and does not broaden post-processing error catches. In the #52 fixture, the solver proceeds to the later measurable candidate and produces a valid length-matched meander.

If no candidate works, the existing named no-solution path remains intact: post-processing returns its best valid completed-stage or original geometry with a diagnostic rather than accepting invented copper. Standalone solver invariant behavior is otherwise unchanged.

## Regression coverage

- convert the #52 integration reproduction from expecting the throw to asserting successful solve, meander output, and matched lengths
- add a direct unit regression proving missing paired same-layer geometry returns `null` without throwing
- update and visually inspect the expected SVG snapshot

## Validation

- `bun test --timeout 9999999` — 80 pass, 0 fail, 843 assertions
- `bun run typecheck` — pass
- `bun run typecheck:structure` — pass (existing folder-count advisories only)
- `bun run build` — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass

title: Fix WASM loading in standalone Node bundles
description: Fixes WASM loading in standalone Node bundles by using embedded WASM bytes instead of requiring a separate manifold.wasm file.
body:
## Summary

- use the existing embedded Manifold WASM as the default in Node as well as browser and worker bundles
- preserve `setWasmUrl()` for consumers that want to emit and serve a separate WASM asset
- add a regression that builds and executes a standalone Node bundle without an adjacent `manifold.wasm` file

## Why this is needed

The package already embeds the Manifold WASM bytes in its JavaScript, but its previous default Node path ignored those bytes and attempted to read a separate `manifold.wasm` from disk. That works when the package is executed unbundled from `node_modules`, where the JavaScript and WASM files remain adjacent.

It fails when a consumer bundles the JavaScript into a standalone Node executable. Bundlers such as Bun include the JavaScript module but do not automatically discover and copy a transitive dependency's runtime WASM file beside the generated entrypoint. Manifold consequently searches for a file that is not present.

The failure surfaced in [tscircuit/cli#4441](https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/4441) after `circuit-json-to-footprinter` began using `@tscircuit/manifold-2d`. Fixing it in the CLI would require dependency-specific code that resolves and copies Manifold's internal asset. WASM initialization is owned by this package, so the robust solution is to pass the existing embedded bytes through Emscripten's supported `wasmBinary` option in the default Node path. Consumers that deliberately want a separate asset can continue using `setWasmUrl()`.

## Verification

- `npm test`
- `npm run test:browser`
- standalone Node bundle regression runs without an adjacent `manifold.wasm`

body:
## Why

Altium stores visible component parameters, pin labels, net labels, and power labels with their own text presentation. The converter previously recreated much of that text with defaults, so real round-tripped schematics lost labels or changed their size, color, alignment, and placement.

## What changed

- Preserve visible component parameters and pin text as component-owned `schematic_text` elements.
- Use a colocated `schematic_text` to preserve the existing presentation of a semantic net label or power label, without duplicating the rendered text.
- Write the preserved size, color, rotation, alignment, placement, and visibility back to the appropriate native Altium records.
- Keep schematic coordinates on the native Altium grid so relative text placement does not drift by one grid step.
- Refresh all five real open-source source-vs-converted SVG snapshots and add a focused native net-label presentation test.

This uses the current Circuit JSON API. The semantic elements still describe the electrical schematic, while existing `schematic_text` elements carry presentation when needed. No schema change or private metadata is involved.

Circuit JSON does not currently store font family, so a source distinction between Arial, Verdana, and Times cannot survive the round trip. The converter preserves every text property the current API represents and does not guess a family.

## Testing

- `bun run check`
- 45 test files passed
- 496 assertions passed
- visually inspected all five real-schematic source/conversion snapshots

description: Why Circuit JSON already represents custom symbols with a schematic_symbol element. A schematic_component references it through schematic_symbol_id, and the existing schematic line, path, circle, arc, and rectangle primitives reference the same symbol ID. The converter did not process that relationship. It therefore ignored the symbol primitives and usually emitted a generic component rectangle instead.  Changes resolve custom primitives through schematic_component.schematic_symbol_id write the existing Circuit JSON line, path, circle, arc, and rectangle primitives as native component-owned Altium records retain component-scoped lookup as a compatibility fallback use the schematic_symbol name for the Altium library reference include symbol primitive extents when sizing the output sheet make the real-Altium test adapter produce the established schematic_symbol relationship add a focused test whose primitives have only schematic_symbol_id, proving that symbol lookup is required update the five real schematic SVG round-trip snapshots No Circuit JSON schema changes are needed. All ellipse records used by these five fixtures have equal primary and secondary radii, so they are existing schematic_circle elements. Two genuinely elliptical arc records are not representable by the current Circuit JSON primitives and remain intentionally skipped rather than approximated. body:
## Why

Circuit JSON already represents custom symbols with a `schematic_symbol` element. A `schematic_component` references it through `schematic_symbol_id`, and the existing schematic line, path, circle, arc, and rectangle primitives reference the same symbol ID.

The converter did not process that relationship. It therefore ignored the symbol primitives and usually emitted a generic component rectangle instead.

## Changes

- resolve custom primitives through `schematic_component.schematic_symbol_id`
- write the existing Circuit JSON line, path, circle, arc, and rectangle primitives as native component-owned Altium records
- retain component-scoped lookup as a compatibility fallback
- use the `schematic_symbol` name for the Altium library reference
- include symbol primitive extents when sizing the output sheet
- make the real-Altium test adapter produce the established `schematic_symbol` relationship
- add a focused test whose primitives have only `schematic_symbol_id`, proving that symbol lookup is required
- update the five real schematic SVG round-trip snapshots

No Circuit JSON schema changes are needed. All ellipse records used by these five fixtures have equal primary and secondary radii, so they are existing `schematic_circle` elements. Rounded rectangles use the existing `schematic_rect` representation. Two genuinely elliptical arc records are not representable by the current Circuit JSON primitives and remain intentionally skipped rather than approximated.

No AltiumTS change is needed; it already parses, serializes, and renders the native records used here.

## Testing

- `bun run check` (43 tests)
- visually reviewed all five source/converted SVG snapshots

body:
## Summary

- preserve byte-for-byte `SimpleRouteJson` captures from the breakout `algorithmFn` boundary for the latest merged consumer PR [#6](https://github.com/0hmX/simplified-am62l-computer/pull/6), merge commit `8063a9a39364d38238a2063d0d6158dec56b0593`
- capture with the pour-only producer correction from Core PR [#3389](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3389), commit `1a914b60f8d12f082c53d85c4ea218591bf5589d`
- retain the full 988-obstacle SRJ, accumulated-trace behavior, 33 fixed-target connections, eight layers, three ordered DDR buses, targets, bounds, and rules
- change only the two RAM `isCopperPour` obstacle objects from SoC bounds to RAM bounds
- keep solver and visualizer algorithms unchanged

## Raw fixtures

- SoC: 9,164,064 bytes, SHA-256 `4ea12abe2d3f55ddc62e3d54ef48a810aa38fefb2dad7d9bc889036111afda2e`
  - byte-identical to the prior correct 988-obstacle fixture at commit `1beb42e`
  - pours: inner1/inner6, center `(2, 1)`, size `21.300000000000004 x 21.300000000000004 mm`
- RAM: 9,164,057 bytes, SHA-256 `824cc9d1f3189b4624631bc7f8d83988d425376447061e82f53a2d629c0fc3e4`
  - 988 obstacles = the same 986 non-pours + 2 corrected GND pours
  - pours: inner1/inner6, center `(29.675, 0.949083)`, size `24.05 x 19.200000000000003 mm`

Each input has 33 connections, three buses, eight layers, zero traces at the captured local boundary, and 11 targets on each of bottom, inner2, and inner5.

## Exact comparison with the prior fixtures

- direct byte comparison of new SoC vs `1beb42e` SoC: identical
- canonical comparison of RAM with `obstacles` removed: identical
- canonical comparison of all 986 RAM obstacles where `isCopperPour != true`: identical
- canonical non-pour SHA-256 for old/new SoC and RAM: `c2a4fbf54853706cfa1d72f14a435f56e309aabb9fa5b3821929b3ba8b15a9b2`
- the only RAM semantic difference is its two pour objects moving from the SoC bounds to the RAM breakout bounds

## Capture method and current failures

A disposable consumer worktree linked `@tscircuit/core` to the locally built corrected Core PR #3389 commit. Each raw argument was serialized at `algorithmFn` entry, before the consumer adapter or `FixedTargetBgaFanoutSolver` constructor, as two-space JSON with its capture newline. The importer validates the hash and parsed shape, then copies the original byte buffer without filtering, normalization, or reserialization.

The SoC was first captured through its natural solver failure. A diagnostic custom-solver zero-trace continuation was then used only to let Core reach the independent RAM phase. The natural and diagnostic SoC captures are byte-identical. No machine-local dependency path is committed.

- SoC still fails in `route_top_layer_dogbones`: 23/33 total, best residual set 10/20
- RAM still reaches `compatibilityRoute` and remains active during the focused five-second bounded subprocess check

## Visualization contract

- each BGA source has one labeled dashed guide to its actual local `pointsToConnect[1]` endpoint
- no visual primitive is produced from `bus.connectionExitTargets`
- no outside marker, segment, hover label, banner, legend, or role annotation is shown
- solver and visualizer routing behavior is unchanged

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`: pass, no dependency changes

title: Detect copper placed inside PCB keepouts
description: Add a placement check for SMT pads, plated holes, and vias overlapping same-layer PCB keepouts, honoring excluded component IDs and deduplicating errors, while supporting rectangular and circular keepout geometries.
body:
## Summary

- add a placement check for SMT pads, plated holes, and vias overlapping same-layer PCB keepouts
- honor `excluded_pcb_component_ids` and deduplicate multiple overlapping pads into one error per component/keepout pair
- support rectangular and circular keepout geometry
- register the check in `runAllPlacementChecks`

## Ownership and routing behavior

This detects a genuine pre-route placement violation: copper that already exists in a footprint (or an explicitly placed via) overlaps a PCB keepout before the autorouter runs. The router cannot legally connect a terminal whose pad is already inside forbidden copper space.

Core already consumes this category through its existing placement gate: `Board_doInitialPcbPlacementDesignRuleChecks` runs `runAllPlacementChecks`, records the `pcb_placement_error`, and `shouldSkipAutoroutingBecauseOfPlacementErrors` prevents routing until the placement is corrected (or placement checks are explicitly disabled).

This is therefore different from a post-hoc validator that rejects otherwise successful autorouter output. The violation exists in the input placement, and the established pre-route gate handles it before any route is produced.

The smart-watch antenna network reproduces the issue: L2/C14 footprint copper enters a keepout that excludes only ANT1.

## Visual regression coverage

- a labeled rectangular-keepout snapshot shows `C14: ERROR` while `ANT1: EXCLUDED` is accepted
- a labeled circular-keepout snapshot shows a shared-layer via violation

## Summary

Bugreport98 contains a legacy `through_obstacle` marker inside an oval pad's rectangular approximation but outside its actual copper. title: Use SRJ clearance for Pipeline9 DRC repair
description: Fixes the inconsistency in Pipeline9 joint-repair clearance by evaluating against the input SRJ minTraceToPadEdgeClearance instead of a hard-coded benchmark.
body:
## Summary
- fix the lone Pipeline9 joint-repair clearance inconsistency by evaluating against the input SRJ `minTraceToPadEdgeClearance` instead of the hard-coded 0.10 mm benchmark preset
- keep the indexed engine and exact reference evaluator on the same declared clearance
- allow targeted callers to override the relaxed DRC preset without changing benchmark defaults

## Scope and architectural fit
This is a narrow Pipeline9 consistency fix. The earlier `globalDrcForceImproveSolver` stage already uses `high-density-repair03`, where `GlobalDrcForceImproveSolver` derives DRC `traceClearance` from `params.srj.minTraceToPadEdgeClearance`. The later Pipeline9 joint-repair stage was the lone outlier: its indexed and reference evaluators still used the benchmark 0.10 mm preset. This PR makes that final stage honor the same SRJ-declared clearance.

Core behavior and autorouter output acceptance are unchanged. This adds no core gate, does not block or reject autorouter output, and does not change benchmark defaults. It only prevents the Pipeline9 joint-repair solver from treating copper that satisfies the board-declared clearance as a repair target.

## Regression
A 0.10 mm trace with 0.060 mm pad-edge clearance is legal when the SRJ declares 0.050 mm. Previously Pipeline9 treated it as an error and could move legal copper into a real violation while reducing its hard-coded issue count.

The smart-watch reproduction changed from 54 synthetic 0.10 mm issues and 11 final board-rule violations to zero pre- and post-power-expansion board-rule clearance errors.

## Validation
- focused Pipeline9 DRC tests: 3 passed
- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- smart-watch three-phase Pipeline9 reproduction: zero clearance errors before and after power expansion

title: Preserve same-net junctions during power expansion
description: Fixes the issue of losing same-net pad, trace, and via contacts during power expansion by ensuring that reroutes preserve these connections, preventing significant connectivity loss in circuit designs.
body:
## Summary

- preserve same-net pad, trace, and via contacts when accepting planar or layer-aware reroutes
- reject local trace pushes that remove an existing same-net copper contact
- turn the MangoPi R3C reproduction into a regression that checks every connection for endpoint-connectivity loss

## Root cause

The planar expander preserved only the two splice endpoints of a rerouted interval. In the MangoPi fixture, an interior portion of source_net_0_mst62_0 touched a large GND pad and acted as the junction between the trace and the rest of the GND tree. A shorter grid route kept the splice endpoints but removed that interior contact, reducing GND connectivity from 95/99 endpoints to 1/99.

The solver now records the external same-net copper objects uniquely touched by a replaced interval and accepts the candidate only when the replacement preserves those contacts. Contact queries use the existing spatial index and exact copper geometry, so the invariant is checked only for successful local candidates rather than by rescanning the whole board on every step.

## Before and after

The captured input starts with 502/518 physically connected endpoints across the board, including 95/99 GND endpoints.

| Metric | Before fix | After fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Physically connected endpoints | 408/518 | At least 502/518 |
| Physically connected GND endpoints | 1/99 | At least 95/99 |
| Junction-breaking grid candidate | Accepted | Rejected before mutation |

The after values are enforced connection-by-connection: no connection may finish with fewer physically connected endpoints than it had in the captured input.

## Validation

- bun test: 49 pass, 0 fail
- exact MangoPi fixture: all 113 connections retain at least their input physical endpoint connectivity; GND retains at least 95/99
- bun run typecheck
- bun run build
- bun run benchmark:rp2040: completed; 85.29% nominal coverage and 0 same-net contact rejections on the RP2040 fixture
- Biome format check on changed files
- git diff --check

## Stack

Stacked on #20, which adds the exact MangoPi R3C reproduction fixture and failing regression. This PR contains the fix and changes that regression to assert connectivity preservation.

description: Summary add an SRJ-native physical connectivity signature and require every expansion, cleanup, clearance-repair, and final checkpoint to preserve the last connected endpoint partition roll unsafe phases back transactionally and keep attempteddiscarded mutation stats separate from geometry that is actually emitted keep connectionless child routing byte-for-byte immutable; electrical aliases affect clearance but never imply mutation ownership detect pre-existing violations on immutable vias without rewriting them, reject every new stable viarulecopper-object violation pair, and report preserved debt as best effort correct first-route-point segment-width splitting so preprocessing cannot silently add or remove copper cover cleanup, budget exhaustion, equal-count component swaps, pads, vias, fixed-trace via identity, jumpers, through-obstacle routes, legacy oval geometry, unsupported ellipses, and output aliasing  Safety contract A candidate may merge physical same-net terminal components, but it may never split a component that was connected at the prior validated checkpoint. Unsupported legal geometry fails closed to exact trace preservation. Public solver output is cloned from the last safe snapshot.
