It does not claim a universal final cross-net, clearance, or board-edge DRC certificate; candidate collision checks still enforce those rules, and the board-wide final DRC signature is tracked in 23.  Validation bun test: 78 passed, 0 failed, 616 assertions MangoPi: 502518 endpoints and GND 9599 preserved through expansion-budget finalization RP2040: 169 assertions; all opaque routes unchanged; owned vias repaired; four pre-existing immutable-via violations reported as preserved debt bun run typecheck bun run build git diff --check Stacked on 20, which now includes merged 21.
body:
## Summary

- add an SRJ-native physical connectivity signature and require every expansion, cleanup, clearance-repair, and final checkpoint to preserve the last connected endpoint partition
- roll unsafe phases back transactionally and keep attempted/discarded mutation stats separate from geometry that is actually emitted
- keep connectionless child routing byte-for-byte immutable; electrical aliases affect clearance but never imply mutation ownership
- detect pre-existing violations on immutable vias without rewriting them, reject every new stable via/rule/copper-object violation pair, and report preserved debt as best effort
- correct first-route-point segment-width splitting so preprocessing cannot silently add or remove copper
- cover cleanup, budget exhaustion, equal-count component swaps, pads, vias, fixed-trace via identity, jumpers, through-obstacle routes, legacy oval geometry, unsupported ellipses, and output aliasing

## Safety contract

A candidate may merge physical same-net terminal components, but it may never split a component that was connected at the prior validated checkpoint. Unsupported legal geometry fails closed to exact trace preservation. Public solver output is cloned from the last safe snapshot.

Immutable-via debt is tracked by stable via, rule, and copper-object pairs, so repairing one baseline collision cannot hide a different collision introduced on the same via. Immutable-only rejection has separate rollback telemetry from physical-connectivity rejection.

This closes the open-circuit class exposed by the MangoPi fixture and the mutation paths left outside #21. It does not claim a universal final cross-net, clearance, or board-edge DRC certificate; candidate collision checks still enforce those rules, and the board-wide final DRC signature is tracked in #23.

## Validation

- `bun test`: 78 passed, 0 failed, 616 assertions
- MangoPi: 502/518 endpoints and GND 95/99 preserved through expansion-budget finalization
- RP2040: 169 assertions; all opaque routes unchanged; owned vias repaired; four pre-existing immutable-via violations reported as preserved debt
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`

Stacked on #20, which now includes merged #21.

## Summary

- preserve paired target coordinates and layers when assigning explicit fanout exits
- route each ordered bus from its initial dense-pad escape via directly to its reserved boundary slot with bounded labeled pathfinding
- keep every trace on one escape layer after that first via, avoiding crossover vias within the bus
- prefer zero additional vias lexicographically while retaining the previous crossover channel as a bounded fallback
- support single-layer and same-layer coordinated buses without changing legacy layerless exit-target behavior

## Why

The AM62L/LPDDR4 repro exposed 38 same-layer endpoint inversions. A straight-line global router therefore had to cross the traces in the middle, even though the permutation can be resolved inside the fanout immediately after escaping the dense pad field.

The new path reserves all source via barrels, existing routed copper, accepted fanout copper, and plane endpoint copper. It validates every exact emitted segment before accepting the complete bus.

## Validation

- AM62L Core repro: both 16-trace fanouts solve with exactly one via per trace
- straight global handoff: zero BYTE0/BYTE1 winding conflicts
- final Core routing checks: zero trace and via-clearance errors
- focused winding tests cover one escape layer, same-layer accepted buses, layer restrictions, legacy targets, and shared boundary bands
- typecheck, Biome, and git diff check pass
- full solver suite: 97 pass; only the known Dataset 07 SVG snapshot mismatch that reproduces on clean main remains

body:
## Summary

- add a canonical FanoutExitPosition API and map edge-first names to local escape direction, boundary band, and physical exit edge
- route orthogonal escapes through reserved boundary channels so rightside_top and rightside_bottom terminate on the right border
- reserve slots and rails across buses and layers, including via-safe terminal spacing and capacity checks
- preserve legacy inferred-corner behavior, plane termination, single-layer routing, and inferred same-bus merging
- validate incompatible or conflicting explicit routing fields

## Why

A corner preference alone cannot distinguish an exit on the top edge near the right from an exit on the right edge near the top. Explicit physical edges let Core produce direct upper and lower DDR breakout interfaces without forcing traces through the BGA field.

## Related

- Props API: https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/812
- A coordinated Core PR will consume both APIs.

## Validation

- full local suite: 90 pass with one known Dataset07 SVG mismatch that is also reproducible without this feature; no new functional failures

description: Preserves the values of Altium title block parameters in the conversion process, ensuring that placeholders are replaced with actual values during schematic import.
body:
## Why

Real Altium title blocks contain references such as `=REVISION` and `=DrawnBy`. Their values are stored separately as hidden document parameters. Our round-trip fixture was putting the reference text into Circuit JSON, so the converted schematic kept placeholders instead of the values shown by Altium.

## What changed

- Pin AltiumTS PR [#69](https://github.com/tscircuit/altiumts/pull/69) by exact commit.
- Resolve native document-parameter references while importing the real Altium schematic fixtures.
- Keep unresolved project/runtime references unchanged because their values are not present in a standalone `.SchDoc`.
- Assert that HERON PAY-SSM preserves revision `v4.3` and its author names rather than the references.
- Assert that HERON systems preserves its sheet numbering rather than `=SheetNumber` and `=SheetTotal`.
- Refresh the two real-board side-by-side SVG snapshots.

Production conversion already preserves normal `schematic_text`, so no Circuit JSON API or converter-specific parameter type was needed. Altium syntax resolution stays in AltiumTS; this repo consumes the resolved text.

The PCB annotation snapshot also refreshes because the newer pinned AltiumTS commit includes the already-merged native dimension rendering.

- 45 test files passed
- 504 assertions passed

title: Export schematic sheets as native hierarchy
description: Creates a root schematic with native Altium sheet-symbol, sheet-name, sheet-file, and sheet-entry records, allowing for proper hierarchical representation of schematic sheets in Altium.
body:
Circuit JSON already represents pages with `schematic_sheet` elements and page boundary ports with componentless `schematic_port` elements. The converter was writing each page as an unrelated `.SchDoc`, so Altium had no root sheet, no child links, and no sheet entries.

This creates one root schematic with native Altium sheet-symbol, sheet-name, sheet-file, and sheet-entry records, then writes each Circuit JSON sheet as the referenced child `.SchDoc`. Unassigned elements remain on the root page. Existing `subcircuit_id` and `is_schematic_group` data is used when an explicit sheet-box position exists; otherwise the root boxes receive a deterministic grid layout. No Circuit JSON API change was needed.

The real HERON PAY and HERON systems fixtures now preserve 23 sheet boxes and 128 entries, including relative box position, size, name, and entry names. The focused multi-sheet test verifies the root links point to real child files and snapshots their entries.

Depends on tscircuit/altiumts#68 for SVG rendering of the native hierarchy records and pins that exact commit until it merges.

Verified with `bun run check`: 45 test files passed with 506 assertions, including all five real schematic round trips.

## Summary

- Discover adjacent, assignable power pads on the selected BGA and connect only exact-same-net pads with legal short top-copper links.
- After mandatory reference signal routing is complete, deterministically dogbone each disconnected cluster into an electrically matching copper pour when a legal through-via site remains.
- Treat power-plane drops as best effort: unresolved clusters receive stable skip metadata and never fail or block later/output stages.
- Emit truthful physical power traces, via spans, and optional plane-connectivity metadata only for successful drops.
- Add two observable stages and visuals: `same_net_pad_clusters` and `copper_pour_via_drops`.
- Promote solid and dashed trace linework above pour/pad fills in the focused BGA visualization while keeping endpoint, via, search, and skipped markers in the foreground.

- Prescribed signals: **33/33** routed with the requested layer distribution.
- Eligible power pads: **58**.
- Power pads connected to matching pours: **50/58**.
- Successful pour drops: **31**.
- Truthful unresolved/skipped clusters: **8** (`no_legal_candidate`), non-fatal.

body:
## Problem

The validated fixed-target algorithm was hidden behind a coarse compatibility stage, and the first visibility split still left the expensive early-drop, top-layer, and prescribed-inner searches atomic. A single debugger step could therefore block for seconds without revealing which candidate, A* node, conflict, or route decision was active.

## What changed

- Rebuilt the public pipeline as 13 truthful stages: `buildFanoutModel`, `sampleFreeSpaceCells`, `discoverFreeSpaceRegions`, `packFreeSpaceRegions`, `rankFanoutNets`, `initializeReferenceRouting`, `placeIndependentEarlyDropVias`, `completeTopLayerRoutes`, `assignPrescribedLayers`, `routePrescribedInnerLayers`, `miterRouteCorners`, `validateReconstructedGeometry`, and `buildOutput`.
- Preserved the proven reference dataflow, ordering, mutation order, deterministic RNG, tie-breaking, and final geometry.
- Converted early-drop candidate/conflict/backtracking work and both top/inner A* searches into resumable generators. One outer solver step now exposes one real algorithm action: candidate legality, conflict/backtrack decision, A* pop, neighbor accept/reject, route/order result, or commit.
- Added an active-compute clock so UI pauses do not consume the existing search budget.
- Added shared semantic A* graphics: large labeled S/T endpoints, a dotted intent guide, a live predecessor-derived candidate path with a contrast halo, the current expanded node, secondary frontier/visited state, concise action/status/reason/progress text, muted inactive ratlines, and distinct layer-aware accepted copper.
- Kept the implementation general. Production code has no fixture names, golden lookup/replay, known coordinates, connection IDs, or fixture-specific branches.

## Correctness and generality

- SoC golden parity: 33 traces, 33 vias, 0 unrouted.
- RAM golden parity: 33 traces, 33 vias, 0 unrouted.
- A translated and renamed 33-connection case exercises early, top, and inner generators on arbitrary runtime names and coordinates, advances through multiple real steps, and completes successfully.
- Existing intentional failure/stall repro tests still assert their documented behavior.

## Local timing profile

Atomic baseline versus incremental outer-step latency:

- Early-drop: SoC 1894.5 ms atomic to 2.659 ms max / 0.007 ms p95; RAM 909.9 ms atomic to 21.943 ms max / 0.004 ms p95.
- Top A*: SoC 8132.6 ms atomic to 2.654 ms max / 0.010 ms p95; RAM 127.7 ms atomic to 1.256 ms max / 0.009 ms p95.
- Inner A*: SoC 6010.0 ms atomic to 4.250 ms max / 0.0053 ms p95 across 3,209,060 actions; RAM 8161.0 ms atomic to 8.038 ms max / 0.00525 ms p95 across 4,114,002 actions.

No playback batching or cached reveal is used. Search observability is the priority.

## Verification

- `bun test --timeout 180000` — 17 pass, 0 fail, 762 assertions in 219.74 s.
- `bun test tests/soc-output-parity.test.ts tests/ram-output-parity.test.ts tests/granular-pipeline-visibility.test.ts tests/generic-translated-progression.test.ts --timeout 180000` — 4 pass, 0 fail, 396 assertions in 78.39 s.
- `bun run typecheck` — pass.
- `bun run format:check` — pass, 66 files checked with no fixes.
- `git diff --check` — pass.

The in-app browser runtime had no connected backend, so representative SoC/RAM top and inner A* frames were rendered through the project-native `GraphicsObject` SVG/PNG path instead. All four frames received local visual review after the hierarchy cleanup.
